data.title: An illustrated guide to automatic sparse differentiation
data.author: mariuz
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种名为自动稀疏微分（Automatic Sparse Differentiation, ASD）的技术，用于加速机器学习中Hessians和Jacobians的计算。尽管自动微分（AD）在机器学习中广泛应用，但ASD尚未普及。文章首先回顾了传统的AD，包括前向和反向模式下的Jacobians计算，然后深入探讨了ASD的两个核心组件：稀疏模式检测和矩阵着色。文章还讨论了稀疏Hessians的计算，并通过实际示例展示了ASD的性能优势，特别是在高维度情况下能够显著降低计算和内存需求。最后，文章提供了性能基准，并指导何时应使用ASD而非传统AD。

主要讨论点：Jacobian矩阵的计算及其在自动微分（autodiff）中的应用

不同观点：
• [gwf] 认为其1999年的NIPS论文对Jacobian的推导和解释更加清晰，提供了一种能够以与标准反向传播相媲美的复杂度来计算Jacobian与任意向量乘积的操作符。他引用了与B.A. Pearlmutter合著的论文作为支持。

• [rdyro] 对博客和可视化表示赞赏，强调了计算稀疏Jacobian在减少计算量方面的优势，尤其是当输入与输出之间缺乏依赖关系时。他还提到通过着色自动发现稀疏性的吸引力，并分享了自己编写的稀疏规则自动微分的小项目以及微软的更严肃的实现。

• [FilosofumRex] 提到Lloyd Trefethen的《Numerical Linear Algebra》是该主题的经典参考书，建议阅读最后一章关于迭代方法的内容。他还指出Gilbert Strang的线性代数书籍对理解相关概念有帮助，并回顾了FORTRAN 77时代的自动微分传统。

43828423.article_content:
An Illustrated Guide to Automatic Sparse Differentiation
In numerous applications of machine learning, Hessians and Jacobians exhibit sparsity, a property that can be leveraged to vastly accelerate their computation. While the usage of automatic differentiation in machine learning is ubiquitous, automatic sparse differentiation (ASD) remains largely unknown. This post introduces ASD, explaining its key components and their roles in the computation of both sparse Jacobians and Hessians. We conclude with a practical demonstration showcasing the performance benefits of ASD.
$$ \newcommand{\colorf}[1]{\textcolor{RoyalBlue}{#1}} \newcommand{\colorh}[1]{\textcolor{RedOrange}{#1}} \newcommand{\colorg}[1]{\textcolor{PineGreen}{#1}} \newcommand{\colorv}[1]{\textcolor{VioletRed}{#1}} \def\sR{\mathbb{R}} \def\vx{\mathbf{x}} \def\vv{\mathbf{v}} \def\vb{\mathbf{e}} \newcommand{\vvc}[1]{\colorv{\vv_{#1}}} \newcommand{\vbc}[1]{\colorv{\vb_{#1}}} \newcommand{\dfdx}[2]{\frac{\partial f_{#1}}{\partial x_{#2}}(\vx)} \newcommand{\J}[2]{J_{#1}(#2)} \def\Jf{\J{f}{\vx}} \def\Jg{\J{g}{\vx}} \def\Jh{\J{h}{g(\vx)}} \def\Jfc{\colorf{\Jf}} \def\Jgc{\colorg{\Jg}} \def\Jhc{\colorh{\Jh}} \newcommand{\D}[2]{D{#1}(#2)} \def\Df{\D{f}{\vx}} \def\Dg{\D{g}{\vx}} \def\Dh{\D{h}{g(\vx)}} \def\Dfc{\colorf{\Df}} \def\Dgc{\colorg{\Dg}} \def\Dhc{\colorh{\Dh}} $$
First-order optimization is ubiquitous in machine learning (ML) but second-order optimization is much less common. The intuitive reason is that high-dimensional vectors (gradients) are cheap, whereas high-dimensional matrices (Hessians) are expensive. Luckily, in numerous applications of ML to science or engineering,
Hessians and Jacobians exhibit sparsity
: most of their coefficients are known to be zero. Leveraging this sparsity can vastly
accelerate automatic differentiation
(AD) for Hessians and Jacobians, while decreasing its memory requirements
. Yet, while traditional AD is available in many high-level programming languages like Python
and Julia
,
automatic sparse differentiation (ASD) is not as widely used
. One reason is that the underlying theory was developed in the AD community, outside of the ML research ecosystem.
With this blog post, we aim to shed light on the inner workings of ASD, bridging the gap between the ML and AD communities by presenting well established techniques from the latter field. We start out with a short introduction to traditional AD, covering the computation of Jacobians in both forward and reverse mode. We then dive into the two primary components of ASD:
sparsity pattern detection
and
matrix coloring
. Having described the computation of sparse Jacobians, we move on to sparse Hessians.
After discussing applications in machine learning, we conclude with a practical demonstration of ASD, providing performance benchmarks and guidance on when to use ASD over AD.
Automatic differentiation
Let us start by covering the fundamentals of traditional AD. The reader can find more details in the recent book by Blondel and Roulet
, as well as Griewank and Walther
.
AD makes use of the
compositional structure
of mathematical functions like deep neural networks. To make things simple, we will mainly look at a differentiable function $f$ composed of two differentiable functions $g: \mathbb{R}^{n} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}^{p}$ and $h: \mathbb{R}^{p} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}^{m}$, such that $f = h \circ g: \mathbb{R}^{n} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}^{m}$. The insights gained from this toy example should translate directly to more deeply composed functions $f = g^{(L)} \circ g^{(L-1)} \circ \cdots \circ g^{(1)}$, and even computational graphs with more complex branching.
The chain rule
For a function $f: \mathbb{R}^{n} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}^{m}$ and a point of linearization $\mathbf{x} \in \mathbb{R}^{n}$, the Jacobian matrix $J_f(\mathbf{x})$ is the $m \times n$ matrix of first-order partial derivatives, whose $(i,j)$-th entry is
\[\big( \Jf \big)_{i,j} = \dfdx{i}{j} \in \sR \, .\]
For a composed function
\[\colorf{f} = \colorh{h} \circ \colorg{g} \, ,\]
the
multivariate chain rule
tells us that we obtain the Jacobian matrix of $f$ by
multiplying
the Jacobian matrices of $h$ and $g$:
\[\Jfc = \Jhc \cdot \Jgc .\]
Figure 1 illustrates this for $n=5$, $m=4$ and $p=3$. We will keep using these dimensions in following illustrations, even though the real benefits of ASD only appear as the dimension grows.
Figure 1: Visualization of the multivariate chain rule for $f = h \circ g$.
AD is matrix-free
We have seen how the chain rule translates the compositional structure of a function into the product structure of its Jacobian matrix. In practice however, there is a problem:
computing intermediate Jacobian matrices is inefficient and often intractable
, especially with a dense matrix format. Examples of dense matrix formats include NumPy’s
ndarray
, PyTorch’s
Tensor
, JAX’s
Array
and Julia’s
Matrix
.

data.title: My sourdough starter has twins
data.author: Tomte
data.article_summary:
本文讲述了作者参与的一个公民科学研究项目，名为“Citizen Science Sourdough Project”，由VUB布鲁塞尔和ETH苏黎世大学合作开展。该项目收集和分析了来自不同参与者的酸面团样本。作者的样本名为“Stinkie”，经过数年后收到了研究结果。报告从四个方面对比了样本：  
1. **双胞样本**：在瑞士、希腊和芬兰找到了与Stinkie完全匹配的样本，尽管气候和面粉类型不同。  
2. **发酵偏好**：Stinkie更酸、更轻，发酵温度较低。  
3. **酸度和年龄**：Stinkie的pH值为3.7，与平均值相近，但年龄为11年，远超平均水平。  
4. **酵母和细菌数量**：Stinkie的酵母和细菌细胞数量高于平均，尤其是**Lactobacillus brevis**细菌和**Saccharomyces Cerevisiae**酵母占主导地位，形成了一种单菌种培养，虽然稳定但风味单一。

研究还提到未来可能会有更详细的分析结果发布。此外，研究人员开发了一个名为Dough-Pro的AI助手，帮助理解数据。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：自制酸面包（sourdough）的过程、技巧、以及与发酵种（starter）相关的问题

不同观点：
• ljf认为酸面包的制作过程简单、便宜，且享受制作过程本身，类似于酿啤酒。他强调了BakeWithJack的简化方法，并提到自己的制作流程，包括12小时发酵和冰箱冷藏。
• uptownfunk分享了自己制作披萨的愉快经历，强调自制发酵种的独特性和适应性，并提到能在短时间内制作多个披萨，是一种社交活动。
• arichard123指出酸面包制作的宽容度高，尝试不同的方法和步骤，如隔夜发酵，仍然可以得到满意的结果，强调了探索和尝试的乐趣。
• philsnow提到了疫情期间自制面包的趋势，并用幽默的方式提到了不同发酵种的年龄问题。
• Aloisius讨论了发酵种中酵母的种类和温度对发酵种的影响，特别是旧金山酸面包中的特定酵母和细菌组合，以及商业酵母的潜在影响。
• vintermann提出了一种幽默的创业想法，即为酵母做基因检测服务，表达了对生物技术服务向普通人开放的愿望。
• p00ter分享了自己使用据称有400年历史的德国发酵种的经历，并对其活力和储存能力表示赞赏。
• yumraj提出了关于不经常烘焙时如何管理发酵种的问题，分享了自己长时间冷藏发酵种的方法，并询问其他人是否注意到发酵种质量的变化。
• aloe_falsa引入了“风土”（terroir）的概念，解释了发酵种的独特性如何受到当地气候、面粉和喂养方式的影响。
• trkaky提到酸面包中只有少数几种细菌和酵母，与普遍认为的多样性形成对比。
• taneliv对芬兰黑麦和小麦产量的主次关系提出了疑问，并指出了一个可能的误解。
• 01100011尝试用菠萝增加野生酵母，但结果是发酵种变得像商业酵母一样活跃且失去了酸味，最终决定重新开始。

补充讨论：
• 酸面包制作的宽容度和多样性被多次提到，尤其是不同方法和步骤的尝试和调整。
• 发酵种的独特性和适应性是一个重要话题，包括气候和面粉的影响。
• 商业酵母的影响和自制发酵种的管理方法也被讨论，涉及到温度和酵母种类的问题。
• 发酵种的保存和管理，特别是在不经常烘焙的情况下，是一个实际操作中的关注点。
• 讨论中还涉及到一些技术细节和数据问题，如不同谷物的产量和酵母种类。

争议焦点：
• 酸面包中酵母和细菌的多样性问题，trkaky的观点与其他评论中隐含的多样性假设形成对比。
• 发酵种的管理方法和效果问题，特别是冷藏时间和喂养频率对发酵种质量的影响，yumraj和p00ter的经历提供了一些实际操作的见解。

43829935.article_content:
A couple of years ago, I participated in a study of the
HealthFerm Citizen Science group
in collaboration with the VUB Brussels and ETH Zurich universities. The study, called the
Citizen Science Sourdough Project
, aimed to collect and map micro-organism samples of sourdough starters with the help of citizens like you and me. As a sourdough bread nut, of course I was more than happy to send a sample. And then years passed and I completely forgot about the research project.
Until yesterday, when I finally received an email with the results of my sample (id
4f6d6
)!
In the first part of the result report, your personal sourdough starter is compared to all the other submissions, by investigating (A) possible “twins”, charted on a map of Europe, (B) fermentation preferences such as temperature and time, (C) acidity and age, and (D) amount of yeast and bacteria cells:
THe personalised result report, part 1.
Since the report is in Dutch, I’ll try to summarize it here for each of the four parts. My starter is called
Stinkie
—which does not really need a translation. When I don’t bake during weekdays, I keep it in the fridge, and I usually feed it rye at a 100% hydratation level meaning equal amounts of flour and water. This means it can get quite tangy and if not well-maintained, well,
stinky
!
Stinkie’s twins
—it looks like in Switzerland three other starter samples exactly match mine! Two more twins live somewhere in Greece and Finland. This is significant for me because the uniqueness of your starter is defined by the local climate, local flour, and the way you feed it to keep it alive. The weather in Greece is much warmer than in Belgium and Mediterranean flour is more nutty and
wheaty
than the ones I have access to, while the reverse is true for that twin in Finland where rye is more predominant than wheat. Perhaps they all use the keep-cool-in-fridge technique? Of course I’m just guessing here: the person maintaining his starter in Finland could just as well rely on imported flour.
Fermentation preferences
—compared to starters with rye meal, mine is more acidic and a lot airier (I sometimes feed it wheat flour), but weights much less. Compared to all starters, mine is kept at a much cooler temperature, and the bread I bake with it is much more acidic (when I can, I proof the dough in the fridge as well).
Acidity and age
—Stinkie’s pH level is
3.7
which is about the same as the average of all other starters, but the average age of all the samples is less than 5 years while mine is supposed to be 11 years old! That’s really cool and I have no idea how they measure that since countless amounts of refreshing must have thrown out and regrown everything?
Yeasts and bacteria
—Stinkie has about
41.69
million yeast cells per gram which is a bit more than your typical starter. I’m happy with that, more rising power! It also has a bit more bacteria than the average:
2.82
billion cells per gram. Perhaps because it’s older than others?
I wonder whether there’s a clear correlation between the last point and the age of the starter. I presume the researchers will be fishing for possible correlations and explaining these results in greater detail in some kind of publication I have yet to find (or is yet to be published).
The second part of the result report zooms in on the yeast and bacterial fingerprints of Stinkie:
The personalised result report, part 2. Bacterial fingerprint on the left, yeast on the right.
The graph shows five different vertical bars containing unique combinations of typical sourdough classes, with the sixth bar being the combination of your own starter. For the bacterial fingerprint, Stinkie most resembles class 3, although it looks like one particular species is completely dominating here:
Lactobacillus brevis
(
89.5%
). I think this has to do with the way I store the starter and the unique humidity/flour type/temperature we all use. I’d like to see a bit more variation here. No typical
San Francisco
sourdough bacteria for me…
As for the yeast fingerprint, something weird happened: it most closely matches sourdough profile 3, but even profile 3 has multiple species, with again one being very dominant. In Stinkie, however, there’s only
one
kind of yeast ever-present: the classic
Saccharomyces Cerevisiae
(
100%
). So while part 1 of the report says that in general there are more micro-organisms present in Stinkie compared to other starters, part 2 reveals that over the years, I somehow have been developing a monoculture? While this does produce consistent results and I know my starter’s behaviour very well, it would be nice to introduce a bit of variation in the flavour palette. I wonder what might happen if I was to feed it twice a day at room temperature for a month or so. How fast would that fingerprint change?
In case the results do not make sense, the researchers developed a multilingual AI assistant called
Dough-Pro
that will help you explore all the different aspects of the data. It sounds fancie

• yumraj提出了关于不经常烘焙时如何管理发酵种的问题，分享了自己长时间冷藏发酵种的方法，并询问其他人是否注意到发酵种质量的变化。
• aloe_falsa引入了“风土”（terroir）的概念，解释了发酵种的独特性如何受到当地气候、面粉和喂养方式的影响。
• trkaky提到酸面包中只有少数几种细菌和酵母，与普遍认为的多样性形成对比。
• taneliv对芬兰黑麦和小麦产量的主次关系提出了疑问，并指出了一个可能的误解。
• 01100011尝试用菠萝增加野生酵母，但结果是发酵种变得像商业酵母一样活跃且失去了酸味，最终决定重新开始。

补充讨论：
• 酸面包制作的宽容度和多样性被多次提到，尤其是不同方法和步骤的尝试和调整。
• 发酵种的独特性和适应性是一个重要话题，包括气候和面粉的影响。
• 商业酵母的影响和自制发酵种的管理方法也被讨论，涉及到温度和酵母种类的问题。
• 发酵种的保存和管理，特别是在不经常烘焙的情况下，是一个实际操作中的关注点。
• 讨论中还涉及到一些技术细节和数据问题，如不同谷物的产量和酵母种类。

争议焦点：
• 酸面包中酵母和细菌的多样性问题，trkaky的观点与其他评论中隐含的多样性假设形成对比。
• 发酵种的管理方法和效果问题，特别是冷藏时间和喂养频率对发酵种质量的影响，yumraj和p00ter的经历提供了一些实际操作的见解。

data.title: What Is "Induced Atmospheric Vibration"?
data.author: belter
data.article_summary: "Induced Atmospheric Vibration" refers to a phenomenon where extreme temperature variations cause anomalous oscillations in very high voltage power lines (400 kV), leading to synchronization failures in electrical systems. This effect, observed during a blackout on the Iberian Peninsula, results from atmospheric conditions like temperature and humidity affecting corona discharges around power lines. These discharges, influenced by environmental factors, introduce fluctuations in the electrical grid's reactance, complicating voltage and frequency control. The oscillations can lead to cascading failures in interconnected power systems, as seen in the widespread disturbances across Europe. Although not extensively documented, this phenomenon highlights the complex interplay between atmospheric conditions and power transmission.

It's likely a cascade. The high temperature expands, stretches and distorts the cables (out of round), local heating creates 'thermals' (moving air pockets), the cable dance/gallop and touch. Short term interruption either trips a circuit, the load causes 'slowing' of the generators ('loss of frequency') or the transient short confuses a frequency monitor, and then more circuits are tripped off because of the low frequency (when low frequency the transformers saturate V/f with high peak currents) so more circuits trip. Boom; Iberia switched off!

Anyone who’s had to build a power system rapidly learns that electricity is not as simple as “electrons move, work gets done”.  Real electrical systems have to deal with issues of reactance and other exciting math-heavy constructs designed to drive you into some other field of study.
Power Grids experience this on an epic scale.  They have to concern themselves with a few needs simultaneously:
ensuring electrical potential doesn’t sag under load (maintaining voltage)
ensuring the integrity of the AC waveform (maintaining frequency)
ensuring the system doesn’t lose too much energy to fighting its own electromagnetic behavior (controlling the power factor)
That last one is the part that is profoundly nonintuitive.  Capacitance and inductance inherent to the system create a sort of inertia in the system that must be fought to provide those other two guarantees. Together they work to create what’s called “reactance”.
Long range lines and the equipment they connect to can have a lot of reactance.  High voltages make it even weirder.
One of the strange things that you don’t experience at lower voltages is “corona discharge”.  Very high electrical potentials cause the air around the conductors to become ionized.  When sufficiently ionized, this creates discharges.
You can see static examples of this natural phenomenon in the form of “Saint Elmo’s Fire”.  This often precedes a lightning strike if the potential difference is extreme enough.
But power transmission systems are not static.  They fluctuate dynamically with the AC waveform.  This causes situations where discharges or perturbation in fields that create them act as a new component of the reactance of the system.
Modeling this is very complicated and very important.  Real power transmission systems have active components that work to provide the above guarantees.  Most of the time, they are modeled well and tune things to keep the voltage and frequency where it should be with a minimum of losses due to reactance.
But these corona discharges are unlike the other two components of reactance, because they are affected by the environment outside of the system.  Consider… what affects the voltages at which ionized air molecules might cause a dishcarge?  Temperature and humidity do.
And now we finally reach the part where “induced atomospheric vibrations” starts to make sense.  When things get hotter or drier, discharges happen more readily.  And when they happen, they tend to happen at a given frequency.

data.title: Everything we announced at our first LlamaCon
data.author: meetpateltech
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Meta公司围绕Llama模型的更新及其在AI领域的战略布局引发讨论，涉及开放源代码、技术细节、市场竞争和具体应用等方面。

不同观点：
• Blitzar认为Llama团队在Meta的元宇宙战略中幸存下来值得祝贺，但现在全公司全力投入AI，元宇宙的愿景似乎被搁置。
• Kennethologist详细列举了Meta在Llama模型上的更新，包括API预览、推理速度提升、生态系统扩展、安全工具和新资助项目，认为这些措施增强了Llama的易用性、安全性和社区支持。
• Mohsen1猜测由于Qwen 3的发布，Meta可能推迟了某些模型的推出。
• Throwaw12认为Meta正在进军AI云服务领域，可能是意识到仅靠社交网络难以保持领先地位，尤其是在AWS、Azure和GCP成功的背景下。
• Ahmedfromtunis质疑Llama模型在实际应用中的优势，表示尚未找到其相对于竞争对手的明显优点。
• Zoobab和Amusingimpala75批评Meta的“开放源代码”策略，认为其模型和训练过程不透明，存在“开放洗白”的嫌疑。
• Hedahet认为Meta在开放源代码方面做了不错的工作，但对其公布的更新列表感到失望，认为内容不够深入且缺乏具体数据支持。
• Wewewedxfgdf询问为何Meta不推出针对特定领域（如计算机编程）的模型，认为这样可以减小模型规模并提高运行效率。
• Nailer指出Llama的许可证并不符合开放源代码的定义，特别是其中的“附加商业条款”和广告条款。
• Andhuman对Meta未发布类似Omni的全能模型感到失望，期待能处理语音输入和输出的功能。
• Logicchains猜测由于Qwen 3的发布，Meta可能暂时推迟了Llama 4的发布以提升其竞争力。
• Scosman在尝试注册Llama API的等待列表时遇到技术问题，遭遇重定向循环。
• Havoc简单表示Meta的时机不佳。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中多次提到Meta的“开放源代码”策略，许多用户对其真实性表示怀疑，认为其在开放性和透明度方面做得不够。
• 关于技术细节的讨论，如推理速度和模型更新，部分用户希望看到更多具体数据和比较基准。
• 市场竞争和Meta的战略转向AI云服务也是讨论的重点，部分用户认为这是Meta在面对其他云服务巨头成功后做出的必然选择。
• 实际应用和用户体验问题也被提及，如注册技术问题和对Llama模型应用场景的疑问。

data.title: Bamba: An open-source LLM that crosses a transformer with an SSM
data.author: shallow-mind
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了IBM Research在解决大型语言模型（LLM）推理效率问题上的最新进展。文中提到，随着对话变长，传统Transformer模型的自注意力机制会导致计算成本以二次方增长，造成延迟和冗余计算。为此，IBM开源了混合实验模型**Bamba**，结合状态空间模型（SSM）和Transformer的优点，显著减少内存需求，提升处理速度和准确性。Bamba模型能够在保持Transformer精度的同时，处理更长的序列并提高推理速度。SSM通过维护压缩的隐藏状态来减少内存开销，而Bamba等混合模型则利用了这一特性，同时保留了Transformer处理局部依赖的能力。文章还提到，IBM即将发布的Granite 4.0模型将包含Bamba的创新技术。

Learn more about Bamba and see benchmark results in this
technical blog post
.
Join the first
vLLM meetup in NYC
on May 7 at the IBM Innovation Studio at 1 Madison Avenue in Manhattan! Hosted by IBM and Red Hat, the event will feature technical talks and discussion on how to optimize LLM inference for performance and efficiency.
The transformer architecture behind today’s large language models has shown an uncanny ability to generate human-like text. Part of its effectiveness comes from its self-attention mechanism, which allows the model to weigh all the words in an input sequence when generating a response.
The problem comes as conversations get longer. Because the model holds the running sequence in memory as it responds, the cumulative cost of generation grows quadratically. If the size of the context window doubles, the cost of processing the context and generating a response doesn’t just double — it quadruples.
This “quadratic bottleneck” is often behind that frustrating lag between asking the model a question and getting an answer. It also creates a lot of redundant computing. By the time ChatGPT popularized the transformer in 2022, researchers were already searching for alternative architectures.
State-space models (SSMs), and transformers interleaved with SSM layers, have emerged as two possible solutions. IBM Research has just open-sourced its first hybrid experiment:
Bamba
, a model that can run as quickly as an SSM and process long sequences as skillfully as a transformer. Many of Bamba’s innovations are part of IBM’s next-generation Granite 4.0 models coming in several months.
By significantly reducing the memory requirements of the transformer’s KV (key value) cache memory, Bamba-9B has shown it can run at least twice as fast as transformers of similar size while matching their accuracy.  “Everything comes back to the KV cache reduction,” says Raghu Ganti, the IBM researcher leading the project. “More throughput, lower latency, longer context length.”
The most important model you’ve never heard of
State-space models come nowhere close to matching the name recognition of transformers, but they’ve been used for decades to model dynamic systems.
“They are the bread and butter of electrical engineering — signal processing, robotics, and control theory,” says Ankit Gupta, an IBM researcher who has played a key role in adapting SSMs to deep learning. “Any field that uses time-series data would use state-space models to analyze it.”
The mathematical equations SSMs are built on can be applied to electrical activity in the brain, the weather, and even the stock market. From a series of observations, an SSM calculates a “hidden state” of fixed size, capturing the essential properties of the system. Think of the state as a summary of the past. When new data comes in, the hidden state gets updated, without increasing its size, along with predictions of what will happen next.
SSMs crossed over to neural networks in 2021, when Albert Gu and his collaborators at Stanford
released S4
, an SSM that applied state variables to language. Like the transformer, and recurrent neural network (RNNs), before it, the SSM was good at processing sequences of words. But it could process long sequences more skillfully than RNNs and much faster than transformers.
While a transformer attends to all the words in the context window when outputting a response, an SSM maintains a compressed hidden state that summarizes past information. This selective retention of information requires less memory overhead and leads to faster inference speeds.
S4 made a splash when it suddenly appeared on
Long Range Arena
, a benchmark for comparing language models by their ability to handle long sequences, but it was difficult to implement. Then an AI resident at IBM, Gupta helped Gu and team simplify the model using
diagonal state spaces
. Their “diagonal” SSM shrank S4’s 1,000 lines of code to 10. Gupta later helped to introduce
a gating mechanism
for filtering out irrelevant information, allowing SSMs for the first time to match the “expressivity,” or sequence-modeling skill, of transformers.
That team also unveiled what may be the first hybrid transformer. “Exploring hybrids made sense,” said Gupta, who now works on IBM’s
Granite Vision models
. “We could use standard attention blocks to handle text with local dependencies while leveraging SSMs to do longer-range contextualization.”
In 2023, Gu, then a professor at CMU, and Tri Dao, at Princeton, unveiled a gated SSM variant —
Mamba2
, which helped to inspire a wave of hybrids, with names like
Samba
and
MambaFormer
. Last year, Nvidia confirmed that these new hybrids could outperform either architecture on their own while dramatically
speeding up inferencing
, culminating in their release of Nemotron-H.

data.title: AirBorne: Wormable zero-click remote code execution (RCE) in AirPlay protocol
data.author: throw0101a
data.article_summary:
Oligo Security Research发现苹果AirPlay协议及其软件开发工具包（SDK）存在一系列漏洞，可能导致多种攻击，包括无点击远程代码执行（RCE）、单点击RCE、访问控制列表（ACL）绕过、本地任意文件读取、敏感信息泄露、中间人攻击（MITM）和拒绝服务（DoS）等。这些漏洞被统称为“AirBorne”，可能被攻击者利用来完全控制支持AirPlay的设备，包括苹果设备和使用AirPlay SDK的第三方设备。

其中，CVE-2025-24252和CVE-2025-24132两个漏洞可被用于制造可传播的零点击RCE攻击，导致恶意软件在本地网络中传播。苹果与Oligo合作修复了这些漏洞，并发布了更新软件。Oligo共报告了23个漏洞，导致17个CVE编号发布。

攻击可能影响MacOS、AirPlay SDK和CarPlay设备，特别是在设备设置为“同一网络上的任何人”或“所有人”时更易受攻击。攻击者可能通过公共WiFi入侵设备，进而通过企业网络传播攻击。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：macOS中AirPlay相关的安全问题，特别是由于root权限和网络协议解析器引发的潜在风险。

不同观点：
• Roguelazer认为，运行一个网络协议解析器作为root权限是不必要的，且存在安全隐患。他指出，Apple在macOS中创建了许多沙盒系统和权限分离的用户，但却让HTTP服务器以未沙盒化的root进程运行，这非常奇怪，可能与DRM有关，但DRM守护进程`fairplayd`是以有限权限的用户运行的。

• m463指出macOS的“随意性”，提到随机AirPlay显示出现在镜像下拉菜单中，并怀疑这是否是一种进入系统堆栈的方式，暗示可能的安全漏洞。

Overview
Â Â Â
TL;DR
Oligo Security Research has discovered a new set of vulnerabilities in Appleâs AirPlay Protocol and the AirPlay Software Development Kit (SDK), which is used by third-party vendors to integrate AirPlay into third-party devices.
The vulnerabilities enable an array of attack vectors and outcomes, including:
Zero-Click RCE
One-Click RCE
Access control list (ACL) and user interaction bypass
Local Arbitrary File Read
Sensitive information disclosure
Man-in-the-middle (MITM) attacks
Denial of service (DoS)
These vulnerabilities can be chained by attackers to potentially take control of devices that support AirPlay â including both Apple devices and third-party devices that leverage the AirPlay SDK.Â
The vulnerabilities and the attack vectors they enable have been named âAirBorneâ by Oligo Security researchers, as the attacks that they make possible are transmitted via wireless networks or peerâto-peer connections, and allow attackers to fully take over devices and use that access as a launchpad for further exploitation.
Oligo has demonstrated that two of the vulnerabilities (CVE-2025-24252 and CVE-2025-24132) allow attackers
to weaponize wormable zero-click RCE exploits
. This means that an attacker can take over certain AirPlay-enabled devices and do things like deploy malware that spreads to devices on any local network the infected device connects to. This could lead to the delivery of other sophisticated attacks related to espionage, ransomware, supply-chain attacks, and more.Â
Because AirPlay is a fundamental piece of software for Apple devices (Mac, iPhone, iPad, AppleTV, etc.) as well as third-party devices that leverage the AirPlay SDK, this class of vulnerabilities could have far-reaching impacts.
For perspective:
While not every Apple device worldwide is vulnerable to RCE via AirBorne, Apple stated in January 2025 that there are 2.35 billion active Apple devices across the globe.Â
In 2018 Apple indicated that there were over 100 million active MacOs users globally.Â Â Â Â
Other Apple devices like iPhones, Apple TV, vision pro are affected by different AirBorne vulnerabilities. Devices like iPhones require users to enable the AirPlay receiver in the phone settings.
Additionally, the number of third-party audio devices that support AirPlay can be estimated in the 10s of millions.
While the exact number of CarPlay-enabled devices is not known, it is widely-used and available in over 800 vehicle models.
Apple and Oligo have worked together to thoroughly identify and address the vulnerabilities with the goal of protecting end-users. Apple has released its latest versions of software to address the vulnerabilities and has allowed time for those devices to be updated. Throughout the responsible disclosure process, Oligo provided Apple with the relevant documentation, processes and code associated with these vulnerabilities.
Oligo disclosed 23 vulnerabilities to Apple in total, leading to 17 CVEs being issued. A complete list and description of these CVEs, as well as specific attack scenarios they enable, can be found below.
Types of Attacks
The vulnerabilities found by Oligo - independently or chained together - can enable a variety of possible attack vectors, including Remote Code Execution (RCE), Access Control List (ACL) and user interaction bypass, Local Arbitrary File Read, Sensitive Information Disclosure, Man-in-the-Middle (MITM) attacks, and Denial of Service (DoS) attacks.
For this document we have chosen to focus on RCE attacks on devices using MacOS, the AirPlay SDK, and CarPlay. In future posts, we may examine other types of attacks and other devices relating to AirPlay.Â Â
Remote Code Execution (RCE) Attacks
Using AirBorne, attackers can achieve RCE on vulnerable devices, based on certain factors, such as Apple and third-party device settings, as well as user preferences.
To provide examples, below are some of the different RCE attacks that are possible for devices configured with different settings.
MacOS - Zero-Click RCE
CVE-2025-24252
is a use-after-free (UAF) vulnerability that can be used as a UAF or manipulated into an âarbitrary freeâ action that enables an attacker to execute code remotely onÂ  MacOS devices.Â
When CVE-2025-24252 is chained with CVE-2025-24206 (user interaction bypass), it allows for a zero-click RCE on MacOS devices that are connected to the same network as an attacker with the AirPlay receiver on and set to the âAnyone on the same networkâ or âEveryoneâ configuration. The vulnerability allows for wormable exploits under these circumstances, given it enables an attack path that can spread from one machine to another with no human interaction.
A potential scenario: a victim device is compromised while using public WiFi, then connects to their employerâs network â providing a path for the attacker to take over additional devices on that network.Â

data.title: Show HN: An interactive demo of QR codes' error correction
data.author: Xiione
data.article_summary: QR码具有内置的纠错功能，即使部分损坏（如边角被遮挡、撕坏或涂画），仍可被扫描。用户可以选择或上传QR码图片进行进一步了解，也可以直接扫描QR码。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对QR码生成与纠错功能探索工具的反馈与建议

不同观点：
• [积极反馈 - 功能有趣且有用]
  ◦ [solardev] 认为工具很酷，并对最大错误率计算和可视化提出进一步的功能建议，比如增加最大可损坏像素数量的计算和控制生成时的纠错级别。
  ◦ [pveierland] 喜欢探索界面，但建议优化用户流程，让进入沙盒模式的步骤更易发现。
  ◦ [myself248] 特别喜欢鼠标悬停查看健康条与QR码数据位的对应关系。
  ◦ [gen3] 强调与QR码块交互和了解错误纠正机制的体验很好，并认为该工具在未来绘制自定义QR码时很有用。
  ◦ [teuobk] 喜欢通过调整位来观察块变化的效果。

• [建设性批评 - 缺少解释和UI问题]
  ◦ [flysand7] 认为工具缺少对QR码结构和错误纠正原理的解释，建议增加逐步交互式引导，比如解释QR码角上的小方块作用，并优化图标设计以提高辨识度。同时指出刷子和颜色变化的交互不明显，用户体验不佳。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：
  ◦ [flysand7] 提出工具虽然有趣但缺乏教育性内容，尤其是对不了解QR码结构和错误纠正的用户来说，交互没有明确指导。
  ◦ 其他用户则更多关注工具的功能实现与交互细节，并未提及教育性内容的缺失。

• 重要论据和例子：
  ◦ [solardev] 举例说明最大错误率计算和生成参数控制，建议通过设置不同纠错级别增加冗余。
  ◦ [flysand7] 提到图标难以区分，并用具体例子说明用户界面和交互设计的问题，比如刷子功能不明显。

• 其他值得注意的讨论点：
  ◦ 用户普遍对工具的互动性和功能表示赞赏，但认为在用户引导和教育性内容上仍有改进空间。
  ◦ [flysand7] 特别指出，对于没有QR码知识的用户，当前的UI设计可能导致困惑，建议重新设计以提高可用性。

data.title: It's School time: Adventures in hacking an old Kindle
data.author: FlyingSnake
data.article_summary:
文章讲述了作者在一个周一早晨因女儿再次上学迟到而感到困扰，随后在浏览Hacker News时发现所有Kindle都可以被越狱，于是决定将家中的旧Kindle改造成一个显示上学准备信息的仪表盘。作者详细描述了越狱Kindle的过程，包括识别型号、安装WinterBreak、设置热修复、安装应用启动器和包安装器，以及通过USBNet包启用SSH访问。在解决SSH连接问题后，作者成功获取了Kindle的root权限。

接下来，作者介绍了如何在Kindle上创建一个显示自定义信息的仪表盘。利用修改脚本和命令，作者实现了在Kindle上周期性显示一张PNG图片。由于Kindle需要8位灰度图像，作者调整了图片格式并通过curl命令获取图片。

最后，作者设计了一个后端API，使用Cloudflare Workers、Hono JS、Cloudflare KV和Bun等工具处理实时数据并生成PNG图片，成功实现了仪表盘的功能。

43822251.article_content:
It was Monday and my daughter was late for the school again. To make things worse, the bus came early by 2 minutes. After rushing and making sure she caught the bus on time, I sat down for my morning coffee and opened up Hacker News. The front page had an interesting entry: “All Kindles can now be jailbroken”. Curiously my old kindle was lying next to me. Was this a sign from the universe? There was only one way to know and thus began my journey to turn my kindle into a get-ready-for-school dashboard.
Level 1: Jailbreaking the Kindle ⛓️‍💥
Jailbreaking the kindle was a relatively easy process. The fine folks at
kindlemodding.org
have created a user friendly guide with easy step by step instructions. The guide is very comprehensive and user friendly so it would be futile for me to repeat the steps here. The
KindModding Discord
community is also a great place to ask for troubleshooting.
In a nutshell the main steps I took to jailbreak my kindle were:
Identify your kindle model.
Install WinterBreak. (Just place the zip file in the kindle and reboot.)
Setup a hotfix, i.e. make sure the jailbreak persists after updates.
Install the Kindle Unified App Launcher and a package installer (MRPI)
Enable SSH on the Kindle using USBNet package.
Network shenanigans ☎️
I hit my first roadblock while setting up SSH access for the kindle. The standard USBNet package did not work for my kindle and after some research I found
USBNetLite
which got the SSH working.
The USBNetlite package enables connection to the kindle using 2 modes:
RNDIS/Ethernet gadget. This shows up as
usbx
(
usb0
in my case)
SSH over network using the IP address assigned by the router. This shows up as
wlanx
(
wlan0
in my case)
[root@kindle us]# ifconfig
lo        Link encap:Local Loopback
inet addr:127.0.0.1  Mask:255.0.0.0
...
usb0      Link encap:Ethernet  HWaddr EE:19:00:00:00:00
inet addr:192.168.15.244  Bcast:192.168.15.255  Mask:255.255.255.0
...
wlan0     Link encap:Ethernet  HWaddr 08:84:9D:7B:9C:F1
inet addr:192.168.2.71  Bcast:192.168.2.255  Mask:255.255.255.0
...
To enable the SSH network I had to do the following steps:
Enable USBNet from the KUAL Menu.
Set the IP address manually to
192.168.15.201
or any address in the
192.168.15.xxx
subnet.
SSH using
ssh 192.168.15.244
(usb0 ethernet interface) or the
wlan0
address assigned by the router.
Enter the password from the
/etc/config
file.
With this I had root access to the kindle 🥷
[root@kindle us]# uname -a
Linux kindle 4.1.15-lab126 #1 SMP PREEMPT Thu Nov 28 11:37:06 UTC 2024 armv7l GNU/Linux
Level 2: Conjuring a dashboard on the Kindle ✨
Kindle OS is stripped down version of Linux running an ancient kernel and old Gnu utilities but no package manager. The kindle has several custom tools that enable the Kindle UI operations, like the custom UI framework called
framework
and it’s side-kick
lab126_gui
. It’s workhorse is
lipc
, a
dbus
style program which is used to issue commands to drive the device operations.
There are several ways to develop an app for a hacked kindle. Some apps like KoReader use the FBInk framework
1
and some use Java applets
2
. I chose the easy path: disable the framework, display a PNG image periodically in full screen mode
3
.
I modified the main
dash.sh
script from the OG repos to match my needs. As it happens with old unmaintained devices, neither
xh
nor
wget
worked for my kindle in the background mode. After some debugging, I finally switched back to plain ‘ol
curl
to fetch the PNG from the backend API.
The script runs in a loop based on a cron schedules:
It stops the kindle UI frameworks and screensavers if they’re running.
It checks if the internet is accessible.
It fetches the PNG image from the server
It displays it fullscreen on the kindle using the
eips
command.
A Note about the image resolution: Kindle needs images in 8-bit Grayscale else it will not be displayed correctly. You will also need to find out the kindle’s display resolution using
eips -i
command. (Mine was 800x600)
I used a dummy image to test the kindle client before moving on to the backend side.
Level 3: The API server in the clouds 🌤️
I designed a backend API that collected the data in real-time data and exported it as a PNG image. For that I wanted a platform that’s always up, supports modern web standards, and has a pleasant developer experience. Cloudflare Developer Platform meets all the criteria and it was a breeze to get started.
I used the following tools/frameworks for my backend.
Cloudflare Workers: The workhorse to process incoming requests and image processing.
Hono JS: A Fast, lightweight JS framework.
Cloudflare KV: To cache network requests for an hour
Bun and TypeScript: I love Zig and Bun is really pleasant to work with.
Weather
I am a big fan of
Merry Sky
and the realtime weather API
Pirate Weather API
that powers it. After getting the API key, it was a matter of few hours to fine tune the data I needed to get current weather data. I loved that Cloudflare secrets make it very easy

data.author: keepamovin
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：黑鹰直升机坠毁事件的原因及相关政策问题

不同观点：
• [keepamovin] 认为事故的主要原因是飞行员分心，并未遵循飞行教官的指示。根据录音，飞行员至少有两次未按照指示操作，尽管她看起来经验丰富且曾多次飞过该路线。该评论还提出了个人生活或职业生涯中的潜在问题是否影响了飞行员的表现。
• [firesteelrain] 关注陆军当时允许在民用空域关闭ADS-B Out的政策，质疑这种做法的合理性，尤其是在和平时期。
• [flowerthoughts] 对飞行路线的设计提出疑问，质疑为什么在机场跑道前有如此低的飞行路径，并认为在穿越机场时保持较高的高度可能更安全。
• [VirusNewbie] 质疑空中交通管制（ATC）为何没有与民航飞行员沟通，认为这是严重的失误。
• [listenallyall] 对飞行教官所说的“他认为空管希望他们左转”这一句进行了深入解读，认为即便飞行员幸存，她可能会辩称自己并没有收到明确的指令，因此需要自行评估情况，这与直接不服从命令有所不同。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是飞行员是否明确收到了左转的指令，以及她未执行该建议是否构成不服从。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是关于政策的合理性，特别是ADS-B Out在民用空域的使用问题。
• 飞行路线和安全高度的设计也是讨论的重点，部分评论对现有设计的安全性提出了质疑。

data.title: New atomic fountain clock joins group that keeps the world on time
data.author: austinallegro
data.article_summary: 美国国家标准与技术研究院（NIST）的科学家们推出了一种新的铯喷泉原子钟NIST-F4，其精度极高，有望成为世界标准时间的主要频率基准。NIST-F4通过测量铯原子的恒定频率来保持时间，其设计使其运行上亿年误差不到一秒。该钟加入了由全球十个国家运行的精英时钟行列，增强了全球时间的稳定性和安全性。NIST-F4不仅用于校准协调世界时（UTC），还通过无线电和互联网分发美国官方时间，广泛应用于电信、金融交易和交通系统等领域。它的推出标志着科学和工程上的重大突破，对现代社会的精密时间测量至关重要。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：原子钟及相关技术的现状与未来发展

不同观点：
• RetroTechie：对小型便携式原子钟感兴趣，提到以前曾有类似香烟盒大小的原子钟，但目前对超精确时间没有实际需求。他关注的是小型化、低功耗的原子钟，而不是大型、笨重的设备。
• geerlingguy：提到从铷原子钟升级到更精确的NIST-F4原子钟，并引入了核钟的概念，认为核钟可能带来更高的精度和稳定性。
• infogulch：详细解释了基于铯原子的原子钟的工作原理，并讨论了核钟的潜在优势，包括更高的精度和更窄的频率交互范围，同时提到核钟技术的实现难度。
• 0cf8612b2e1e：关注原子钟的同步问题，质疑在极高精度下如何避免在时钟同步过程中引入误差。
• algorithmsRcool：强调了时间测量的精度已经超过了其他物理量的测量精度，并引用了NIST的数据来说明光学晶格钟的超高精度。

补充讨论：
• CGMthrowaway：提到阿罕布拉宫的狮子钟，将讨论引向历史和文化背景下的钟表艺术。
• WarOnPrivacy：提供了NIST铯喷泉钟的解释链接，增加了讨论的技术背景。
• throw0101a：质疑时钟精度的“极限”在哪里，提出是否存在实际应用需要进一步提高精度，讨论了精度提高的边际效益。

New Atomic Fountain Clock Joins Elite Group That Keeps the World on Time
April 28, 2025
Share
Facebook
Linkedin

NIST scientists have published results establishing a new atomic clock, NIST-F4, as one of the world’s most accurate timekeepers, priming the clock to be recognized as a primary frequency standard — the ultimate source of time.
The NIST-F4 clock was carefully and painstakingly assembled and tested over the last few years.
By joining a small group of elite clocks run by a handful of countries, NIST-F4 makes the foundation of global time more stable and secure.
NIST scientists Greg Hoth (left) and Vladislav Gerginov work on NIST-F4, NIST’s new cesium fountain clock.
Credit:
R. Eskalis/NIST
Clocks on Earth are ticking a bit more regularly thanks to NIST-F4, a new atomic clock at the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) campus in Boulder, Colorado.
This month, NIST researchers published a
journal article
establishing NIST-F4 as one of the world’s most accurate timekeepers. NIST has also submitted the clock for acceptance as a primary frequency standard by the International Bureau of Weights and Measures (BIPM), the body that oversees the world’s time.
NIST-F4 measures an unchanging frequency in the heart of cesium atoms, the internationally agreed-upon basis for defining the second since 1967. The clock is based on a “fountain” design that represents the gold standard of accuracy in timekeeping. NIST-F4 ticks at such a steady rate that if it had started running 100 million years ago, when dinosaurs roamed, it would be off by less than a second today.
By joining a small group of similarly elite time pieces run by just 10 countries around the world, NIST-F4 makes the foundation of global time more stable and secure. At the same time, it is helping to steer the clocks NIST uses to keep official U.S. time. Distributed via radio and the internet, official U.S. time is critical for telecommunications and transportation systems, financial trading platforms, data center operations and more.
NIST-F4 has improved time signals that are “used literally billions of times each day for everything from setting clocks and watches to ensuring the accurate time stamping of hundreds of billions of dollars of electronic financial transactions,” said Liz Donley, chief of the Time and Frequency Division at NIST.
Introducing NIST-F4: The Nation's New Primary Frequency Standard
NIST-F4 isn’t just a clock — it’s the culmination of decades of scientific ingenuity, engineering breakthroughs, and an unwavering pursuit of precision. In this video, we explore the creation of NIST-F4, the United States’ latest primary frequency standard, and how it redefines what it means to measure time with atomic accuracy. From unexpected flaws to groundbreaking redesigns, this is the story of how one of the most precise timekeeping instruments ever built came to be — and why it’s crucial for everything from global synchronization to tomorrow’s technologies. Because when it comes to time, every billionth of a second counts. Find out more:
https://www.nist.gov/atomic-clocks
A Special Kind of Clock
Cesium fountain clocks such as NIST-F4 are a type of
atomic clock
— a complex, high-precision device that extracts timing pulses from atoms. These clocks play a critical role in our globally connected society: They serve as “primary frequency standards” that work together to calibrate Coordinated Universal Time, or UTC (an agreed-upon system for keeping time using data from atomic clocks around the world, known as a time scale).
National measurement labs such as NIST produce and distribute versions of UTC using their own time scales; NIST’s version, for example, is known as UTC(NIST). Those national time scales are then used to synchronize the clocks and networks we rely on in our daily lives.
Read more about how global timekeeping works.
In fountain clocks, a cloud of thousands of cesium atoms is first cooled to near absolute zero using lasers. Then, a pair of laser beams toss the atoms gently upward, after which they fall under their own weight.
During their journey, the atoms pass twice through a small chamber full of microwave radiation. The first time, as the atoms are on their way up, the microwaves put the atoms into a quantum state that cycles in time at a special frequency known as the cesium resonant frequency — an unchanging constant set by the laws of nature.

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AWS成本分析MCP服务器及其相关技术实践与许可问题

不同观点：
• **ponywombat** 提到AWS创建了自己的成本分析MCP服务器，并提供了GitHub链接。这表明AWS正在积极开发和提供相关工具以帮助用户进行成本分析。

• **_pdp_** 对生产环境中凭据散布在配置文件中的做法提出质疑。他认为这种模式可能会引发问题，尤其是在MCP服务器的示例中鼓励这种做法的情况下。这反映了对安全实践的关注。

• **mdaniel** 对特定实现方式（vantage-mcp-server）的工作原理表示疑问，并对许可文本表示质疑，认为其可能针对特定用户群体采取了限制性措施。这暗示了对许可协议和使用场景的潜在担忧。

• **andrenotgiant** 探讨了通过Vantage连接LLM与直接使用AWS成本和使用API的区别，试图理解不同连接方式的技术和实用差异。

• **cat-whisperer** 关注资源交织和标准化问题，询问是否能标准化处理不同资源的成本分析，还是只能根据情况个别处理。

• **salynchnew** 以讽刺的语气指出，云账单的复杂性曾被视为防止AI失控的保护措施之一，而现在只能依赖糟糕的IAM用户体验。这反映了对云服务安全性和用户体验的批评。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是生产环境中凭据管理的安全性，以及现有MCP服务器示例是否鼓励了不安全的实践（_pdp_的观点）。
• 另一个值得注意的点是对特定工具（vantage-mcp-server）的许可协议和使用场景的质疑，尤其是其对不同用户群体的适用性和限制（mdaniel的观点）。
• 技术实现上的差异和标准化问题也是讨论的重点，涉及到如何有效连接LLM与AWS API，以及如何在不同资源间实现成本分析的标准化（andrenotgiant和cat-whisperer的观点）。
• 最后，对云服务安全性和用户体验的总体批评为讨论增添了对更大图景的思考（salynchnew的观点）。

data.title: Researchers are studying how to minimize human impact on public lands
data.author: droptext
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了美国自然保护区在面对大量游客时的管理挑战，特别是科罗拉多州的14,000英尺以上高峰区域。尽管这些荒野地区看似原始，但其实由公园管理员和专家精心管理，以平衡自然保护与游客体验。传统上，管理游客数量的方法包括预约、许可和收费等限制性措施，但现代管理者更倾向于首先通过行为引导来减少游客对环境的影响。近年来，研究人员采用基于证据的方法，利用调查、访谈和无人机等技术研究政策影响，以制定更公平且有效的限制措施。文章还提到，在南 colony 盆地，美国林务局通过改变步道起点和限制露营等方式尝试减少游客影响，但公众对收费的反对使得该方案未能实施。如今，林务局更注重间接管理方法，例如修建引导性的步道以保护脆弱环境。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：国家公园和自然区域的过度拥挤问题及其管理

不同观点：
• **社交媒体导致过度拥挤**：_fat_santa 认为社交媒体是国家公园人满为患的主要原因。他举例说明某些景点因为病毒式传播而变得异常拥挤，而相似的景点却被人忽视。他提到他和家人因此制定了"反社交规则"，避免去那些在社交媒体上非常火爆的地方。

• **人类活动对野生动物的影响**：josefresco 分享了自己在黄石公园的经历，目睹了人们因追逐野生动物而可能对其造成伤害。他提到当时人们不顾危险超车，而公园管理员不在附近，这种行为对动物和人类都可能造成创伤。

• **公园管理的科学方法和基础设施问题**：xtiansimon 强调了科学管理和有效方法的必要性，特别是在面对日益增加的访客和环境压力时。他比较了纽约和宾夕法尼亚州的露营体验，指出未管理的营地卫生状况堪忧，而宾夕法尼亚州的预订系统和设施管理较好。

• **土地归还和原住民权益**：charlescearl 通过链接引入了土地归还的议题，强调了原住民权益和国家公园土地管理的历史问题。

• **阶级和文化对公园使用的影响**：motohagiography 认为公园和自然区域的使用问题本质上与阶级和文化有关。他指出，过去主要是徒步和骑行爱好者使用公园，而现在许多人只是为了寻找便宜或免费的社交和家庭聚会空间，这导致了管理上的挑战，并建议可能需要采用类似其他国家的半私人化政策。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：如何平衡公园的开放性和环境保护，以及如何在管理上创新以适应现代需求。有人认为预订和收费系统是有效的管理工具，但也有人质疑这些措施是否公平和可行。

• **管理措施的例子**：提到宾夕法尼亚州的预订系统通过引导游客选择不同的露营点来减少环境压力，以及纽约地区一些营地卫生设施不足的问题。

• **文化与行为的转变**：讨论了人们使用公园和自然区域的方式发生了变化，从过去的积极运动转向更多的静态社交活动，这给管理带来了新的挑战。

总的来说，评论主要围绕国家公园的过度拥挤、人类活动对环境的影响、管理措施的有效性以及文化和社会因素对公园使用的影响展开讨论。

used to think the Crestone Needle, a jagged peak in Colorado’s Sangre de Cristo range, was unclimbable. Until, that is, Albert Ellingwood and Eleanor Davis reached its summit in 1916. Looking down, they saw a basin whose pristine nature was marred only by their own camp. The Needle was the last of Colorado’s 14ers — peaks higher than 14,000 feet — to be climbed on record.
Today, Ellingwood and Davis would have company up there. In the South Colony Basin, the wilderness area below the Needle, thousands of hikers each year take in the alpine lakes and the jutting rockfaces above. More than 250,000 people try to summit one of the 50-plus Coloradan 14ers annually.
Related
The Science of Search and Rescue
With those crowds come heavy foot traffic, fire rings, litter, and human waste. Leaving no trace can be a lofty goal in the face of such encroachments.
While
wilderness
experiences may seem, well, wild, they are often carefully curated by park and forest service rangers, recreation experts, and others who control access and build infrastructure like trails and install trash cans at trailheads. These professionals research and implement policy choices — large and small — that shape the topography of wildlands’ use. And those professionals have to figure out how best to balance coercive conservation policies with gentle nudges.
Historically, that balance has often involved limiting the number of visitors, through requiring reservations or permits, for instance, or charging fees.
Such impositions were once land agencies’ go-to methods of crowd control. But modern land managers generally like to think of visitor caps, which make the land of the free less free, as a last resort. After all, making the natural world accessible to more people can lead to more people caring about that world, and should — at least in theory — help conservation efforts. Instead, today’s recreation researchers said, they first focus on getting visitors to change their behavior to have less impact on the landscape. When behavioral shifts aren’t enough, though, they still have to figure out which crowd-control strategy serves the most visitors the most fairly, while minimizing their environmental consequences.
While wilderness experiences may seem, well, wild, they are often carefully curated by park and forest service rangers, recreation experts, and others who control access and build infrastructure.
In recent years, crowd control has become more of a science than an art, as a new generation of researchers has nudged the field toward more evidence-based approaches. Through survey studies, structured interviews, and data from remote sensing technology like drones, a growing body of research is analyzing policy impacts on both ecosystems and visitors, digging into the effectiveness of less-restrictive rules, and revealing how to enact restrictions in the fairest way possible.
That work has an impact on the real world more quickly than a lot of other science. “You do a study, and within five or 10 years, you’re seeing that implemented on the ground, and seeing how the data is being used,” said Will Rice, an assistant professor in the department of society and conservation at the University of Montana. “And that’s always really exciting.”

ebates around
how best to manage crowds while
protecting
, say, porcupines and alpine plants aren’t always simple or straightforward. Take the South Colony Basin, where to shrink visitation’s effects in 2007, the U.S. Forest Service decided to move the trailhead 2.5 miles down, restrict backcountry camping locations, and ban campfires in certain areas — all examples of direct land management strategies that use compulsory rules to change people’s interactions with the wild.
After all that, though, the Forest Service still considered charging a fee for visitors. Public opposition to the fee helped cork the proposal.
Since then, the Forest Service has, instead, prioritized more indirect management methods, which encourage but don’t compel good behavior. They build trails through delicate, steep, and rocky parts of the alpine environment so that people will stay the preset course. Thoughtful trails might, for instance, veer hikers’ trajectory toward a good view, so that they don’t have to high-step off-trail to see it.

• **社交媒体导致过度拥挤**：_fat_santa 认为社交媒体是国家公园人满为患的主要原因。他举例说明某些景点因为病毒式传播而变得异常拥挤，而相似的景点却被人忽视。他提到他和家人因此制定了"反社交规则"，避免去那些在社交媒体上非常火爆的地方。

• **人类活动对野生动物的影响**：josefresco 分享了自己在黄石公园的经历，目睹了人们因追逐野生动物而可能对其造成伤害。他提到当时人们不顾危险超车，而公园管理员不在附近，这种行为对动物和人类都可能造成创伤。

• **公园管理的科学方法和基础设施问题**：xtiansimon 强调了科学管理和有效方法的必要性，特别是在面对日益增加的访客和环境压力时。他比较了纽约和宾夕法尼亚州的露营体验，指出未管理的营地卫生状况堪忧，而宾夕法尼亚州的预订系统和设施管理较好。

• **土地归还和原住民权益**：charlescearl 通过链接引入了土地归还的议题，强调了原住民权益和国家公园土地管理的历史问题。

• **阶级和文化对公园使用的影响**：motohagiography 认为公园和自然区域的使用问题本质上与阶级和文化有关。他指出，过去主要是徒步和骑行爱好者使用公园，而现在许多人只是为了寻找便宜或免费的社交和家庭聚会空间，这导致了管理上的挑战，并建议可能需要采用类似其他国家的半私人化政策。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：如何平衡公园的开放性和环境保护，以及如何在管理上创新以适应现代需求。有人认为预订和收费系统是有效的管理工具，但也有人质疑这些措施是否公平和可行。

• **管理措施的例子**：提到宾夕法尼亚州的预订系统通过引导游客选择不同的露营点来减少环境压力，以及纽约地区一些营地卫生设施不足的问题。

• **文化与行为的转变**：讨论了人们使用公园和自然区域的方式发生了变化，从过去的积极运动转向更多的静态社交活动，这给管理带来了新的挑战。

总的来说，评论主要围绕国家公园的过度拥挤、人类活动对环境的影响、管理措施的有效性以及文化和社会因素对公园使用的影响展开讨论。

data.title: WorldGen: Open-source 3D scene generator for Game/VR/XR
data.author: ziyangxie
data.article_summary: WorldGen是一款强大的3D内容生成工具，支持通过简单的文本提示在数秒内生成详细的3D场景。它同时支持文本和图像输入，并允许360°自由探索生成的场景。其工作原理分为两个阶段：首先生成高分辨率的360度全景图，然后将全景图转换为完整的3D场景，支持互动探索。用户可以通过GitHub仓库访问代码，开始创建自己的3D场景。示例包括现代客厅、水下城市、工厂废墟等各种场景。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对某款生成工具的评价与期望

不同观点：
• [atrus] 认为该工具生成的模型缺乏可编辑性，尤其是在需要对细节（如移动某个物体）进行修改时，现有工具不够方便。他期望生成中间文件（如.blend、Godot项目文件等），以便进行更精细的编辑。
• [socalgal2] 对工具的3D生成能力感到失望，指出该工具生成的并非完整的3D场景，而是一个基于全景的网格，当移动出全景中心时，被遮挡的部分会消失。她期望未来的版本能够自动补全场景。
• [firtoz] 对多种生成世界的方法表示欢迎，并分享了他们使用Claude 3.7生成Lua脚本来定义场景的类似尝试。他提到正在关注其他工具（如Meta、Krea）的进展，并计划尝试这些方法。
• [doshaa] 对当前AI项目的过度宣传表示担忧，认为许多项目在实际效果上不如宣传所说的那样好，他希望有更明确的警示和功能按钮，以避免用户的不便。
• [whywhywhywhy] 认为该工具在当前状态下声称可用于游戏、VR、XR等领域是夸大其词，因为工具生成的内容在移动视角时会出现问题，只能用于固定位置的VR或非交互背景。

补充讨论：
• [pedalpete] 对该工具表示兴奋，并提到自己创办的3D场景生成器曾经获得关注，认为结合AI生成场景是未来的趋势。
• [jimmySixDOF] 对工具的开源和整合表示赞赏，并建议在HuggingFace空间上进行克隆。
• [pdntspa] 联想到Cyberpunk 2077的braindances，认为该工具的输出结果与此类似。
• [shihabkhanbd] 对网页内容感到困惑，原以为是一个AI图像生成器。
• [ziyangxie] 提到对网页布局进行了移动端优化。
• [Ono-Sendai] 认为该工具生成的并非真正的3D，而是2.5D。
• [ivape] 关心工具对硬件的要求，特别是Nvidia显卡的显存需求。

争议焦点：
• 该工具是否能被称为“世界生成器”，部分用户（如[whywhywhywhy]）认为其当前功能与宣传不符，尤其是在3D场景生成和交互性方面存在不足。
• 对AI生成项目的实际效果和宣传之间的差距，部分用户（如[doshaa]）表示担忧，并希望有更明确的用户指引和功能说明。

Learn about the technology behind WorldGen's 3D scene generation.

data.title: What It Takes to Defend a Cybersecurity Company from Today's Adversaries
data.author: gnabgib
data.article_summary:
文章总结：

SentinelOne最近几个月观察并抵御了多种攻击，包括出于经济动机的犯罪软件攻击和高级国家支持的攻击活动。这些攻击针对一家美国网络安全公司，攻击者包括：假扮求职者的朝鲜IT人员、试图滥用平台的勒索软件操作者，以及针对与公司业务和客户群一致的组织的中资支持攻击者。

文章强调，网络安全供应商本身是一个关键但少讨论的攻击面。作为高价值目标，SentinelOne不仅帮助客户防御攻击，自身也面临同样的威胁。文章披露了朝鲜IT人员试图通过虚假身份申请公司职位的详细情况，这些人员不断改进策略，使用 stolen 或伪造的身份，试图渗透到公司内部。

通过情报驱动的互动，SentinelOne开发了识别和应对这些威胁的流程，以提高整体防御能力。文章呼吁业界加强协作，提升整体防御水平。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：评论者对SentinelOne相关内容及其表达方式的看法，以及对网络安全行业的讨论。

不同观点：
• [dubbel] 最初以为内容涉及Chris Krebs事件及现任政府，但实际上是关于不同国家背景的黑客活动。这暗示了对标题和内容预期的误解。
• [sublimefire] 认为文章内容较为浅显，仅提及了一些工具（如goreshell, shadowpad, scatterbrain），目标读者可能是企业高管而非分析师或安全人员，意在让读者感到自己难以应对安全问题，从而寻求SentinelOne的帮助。
• [CyberMacGyver] 认为在RSA会议期间，这类网络安全内容的出现很正常，暗示对这种时机的选择持平常态度。
• [ganoushoreilly] 怀疑文章是由ChatGPT编写或改写的，因为使用了大量破折号，暗示对文章的原创性和写作风格不满。
• [PeterStuer] 以讽刺口吻质疑文章内容，暗示对文章中提到的对手（如DPRK）的优先级和真实性持怀疑态度。
• [mediumsmart] 认为不需为培训付费，保持低成本是关键，显示出对成本控制的重视。
• [looperhacks] 提出如何识别敌对势力的IT工作者的问题，反映出对企业是否具备网络安全能力的担忧。
• [gitroom] 认为黑市活动与官方安全措施并行，质疑是通过技术还是通过更聪明的人来堵住安全漏洞，显示出对安全本质的思考。
• [mikewarot] 认为Windows、Linux、MacOS等系统设计上存在安全缺陷，无法完全保障安全，主张使用基于能力的操作系统和数据二极管策略，显示出对现有操作系统安全性的悲观态度和对替代方案的建议。
• [motohagiography] 认为文章提醒了设立前线公司购买安全服务和软件以进行逆向工程和竞争分析是常态，反映出对黑市服务经济的关注。
• [hulitu] 以讽刺语气指出文章未提到俄罗斯或伊朗，暗示对文章选择对手的不满或认为其不全面。

补充讨论：
评论中涉及多个层面的讨论，包括对文章内容深度的质疑、对网络安全服务和工具的实用性、以及对不同国家背景黑客活动的关注。此外，评论者还讨论了黑市活动、系统安全的本质问题以及企业应对安全威胁的实际能力。争议的焦点在于文章的真实性、目标读者以及对不同国家黑客活动的选择性描述。

Adversary
Top Tier Target | What It Takes to Defend a Cybersecurity Company from Today’s Adversaries
Tom Hegel
,
Aleksandar Milenkoski
&
Jim Walter
/
April 28, 2025
Executive Summary
In recent months, SentinelOne has observed and defended against a spectrum of attacks from financially motivated crimeware to tailored campaigns by advanced nation-state actors.
These incidents were real intrusion attempts against a U.S.-based cybersecurity company by adversaries, but incidents such as these are neither new nor unique to SentinelOne.
Recent adversaries have included:
DPRK IT workers posing as job applicants
ransomware operators probing for ways to access/abuse our platform
Chinese state-sponsored actors targeting organizations aligned with our business and customer base
This report highlights a rarely-discussed but crucially important attack surface: security vendors themselves.
Overview
At SentinelOne, defending against real-world threats isn’t just part of the job, it’s the reality of operating as a cybersecurity company in today’s landscape. We don’t just study attacks, we experience them firsthand, levied against us. Our teams face the same threats we help others prepare for, and that proximity to the front lines shapes how we think, and how we operate. Real-world attacks against our own environment serve as constant pressure tests, reinforcing what works, revealing what doesn’t, and driving continuous improvement across our products and operations. When you’re a high-value target for some of the most capable and persistent adversaries out there, nothing less will do.
Talking about being targeted is uncomfortable for any organization. For cybersecurity vendors, it’s practically taboo. But the truth is security vendors sit at an interesting cross-section of access, responsibility, and attacker ire that makes us prime targets for a variety of threat actors, and the stakes couldn’t be higher. When adversaries compromise a security company, they don’t just breach a single environment—they potentially gain insight into how thousands of environments and millions of endpoints are protected.
In the past several months alone, we’ve observed and defended against a spectrum of attacks ranging from financially motivated crimeware to tailored campaigns by advanced nation-state actors. They were real intrusion attempts targeting a U.S.-based cybersecurity company — launched by adversaries actively looking for an advantage, access, or leverage. Adversaries included DPRK IT workers posing as job applicants, ransomware operators probing for ways to access/abuse our platform, and Chinese state-sponsored actors targeting organizations aligned with our business and customer base.
We are certainly not the only ones facing these threats. In the spirit of furthering collective defenses and encouraging further collaboration, we’re pulling back the curtain to share some of what we’ve seen, why it matters, and what it tells us about the evolving threat landscape—not just for us, but for every company building and relying on modern security technology.
DPRK IT Workers Seeking Inside Jobs
One of the more prolific and persistent adversary campaigns we’ve tracked in recent years involves widespread campaigns by DPRK-affiliated IT Workers attempting to secure remote employment within Western tech companies– including SentinelOne.
Early reports
drew attention to these efforts and
our own analysis
revealed further logistical infrastructure to launder illicit funds via Chinese intermediary organizations. However, neither gave a sense of the staggering volume of ongoing infiltration attempts. This vector far outpaces any other insider threat vector we monitor.
These actors are not just applying blindly — they are refining their process, leveraging stolen or fabricated personas, and adapting their outreach tactics to mirror legitimate job seekers in increasingly convincing ways. Our team has tracked roughly 360 fake personas and over 1,000 job applications linked to DPRK IT worker operations applying for roles at SentinelOne — even including brazen attempts to secure positions on the SentinelLabs intelligence engineering team itself.
Public reporting of DPRK IT workers applying to threat intelligence positions
Engagement and Adversary Interaction
Instead of staying passive, we made a deliberate choice towards intelligence-driven engagement. In coordination with our talent acquisition teams, we developed workflows to identify and interact with suspected DPRK applicants during the early phases of their outreach. This collaboration was key. By embedding lightweight vetting signals and monitoring directly into recruiting processes — without overburdening hiring teams — we were able to surface anomalous patterns tied to DPRK-affiliated personas piped directly into our Vertex Synapse intelligence platform for analyst review.

data.title: Linux in Excel
data.author: radeeyate
data.article_summary: **LinuxInExcel** 是一个在 Excel 中运行 Linux 的项目，利用 **mini-rv32ima** 模拟器实现。该模拟器作为一个独立的 DLL 文件，通过 VBA 宏进行调用，将输出结果写入电子表格单元格中。尽管项目存在许多 bug，且作者并未花费过多时间完善，但其目的是为了好玩和实现 Linux 在 Excel 中的运行。构建 DLL 需要使用 MSVC，命令为 `cl dllmain.c /LD /Fefun.dll`，并在 Excel 文件中修改 DLL 的路径。项目代码主要使用 C 语言编写。

Linux In Excel
Linux running in Excel
How?
It makes use of
mini-rv32ima
.
The emulator is built as a seperate dll which is loaded by the VBA macro. The VBA macro calls the emulator in the dll and gets the output and writes it into the cells in the spreadsheet.
The thing is evidently very buggy but I did not want to spend a lot of time on it. This was done mostly for fun. Evidently this was cheating since I did not rewrite the emulator in VBA or Excel formulas but again I wanted to run Linux in Excel and this was one way to do so.
Building and Running
I was using MSVC to build the dll.
Use the following command
cl dllmain.c /LD /Fefun.dll
Then in the Excel file change the path to the dll.

data.title: Mission Impossible: Managing AI Agents in the Real World
data.author: dtagames
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了在快速变化的AI工具环境中，如何有效管理和控制AI代理以实现更好的软件开发成果。作者分享了多个实践技巧，包括选择合适的工具、制定计划、设定规则以及控制成本等。文章强调，AI工具的变化速度远超人类适应能力，因此需要精心规划和限制AI代理的行为范围。关键在于提供高质量的输入材料（代码、提示等），并深入了解所用工具的功能和更新。此外，成功的AI应用还需要开发者具备深厚的架构洞察力和用简单语言表达复杂概念的能力，非专业人员难以利用这些工具创造高质量成果。
data.comments_summary:

   - 支持该方法在企业中的广泛应用，认为通过“计划”或“规则”编码整个应用程序的背景，可以更快速地进行重构以应对新的业务需求。
   - 该方法使得开发人员更具可替代性，因为知识被编码在项目的markdown文件中，新加入的开发者可以通过对代码库提问和追溯历史决策来快速上手。

43832662.article_content:
Mission Impossible: Managing AI Agents in the Real World
David Bethune
Follow
35 min read
·
6 days ago
--
2
Listen
Share
We are at a new frontier with AI tools in every industry, and particularly in software development. They are changing underneath us faster than any human can adapt, and charging us for the privilege. Maintaining control of these robots feels like an impossible mission. Today I’ll share some battle-tested techniques that you can use to rein in your AI agents, chats, and other tools.
This article is part of my
AI Library
. If you’re new to agentic coding, start with
License to Kill
. To dig deep into why and how this stuff works the way it does, check out
Something from Nothing
.
License to Kill: Coding with Cursor AI Agents
Cursor, an AI code writing and editing tool, represents a significant advance in the practical use of artificial…
levelup.gitconnected.com
Something From Nothing
A Painless Approach to Understanding AI
levelup.gitconnected.com
Your Mission
After many successes and failures I’ve had with AI agents, the mission comes down to careful planning and restraining the context of what your agents can do.
Everything that can be done wrong, I’ve done wrong.
If you can set the right guidelines, agents can deliver better results. Everything than can be done wrong, I’ve done wrong and learned from it. It should be no surprise that agents write software this way. Humans do, too, and that’s where agents get their ideas.
Choosing Your Tools
Choosing What to Work On
Finding a Route
Making a Plan
Revising the Plan
Testing the Plan
Finding Bigger Problems
Making Rules
Performance Payback
Choosing Models
Cost Controls
Model Context Protocol (MCP)
Fair Warning:
All screenshots and UI mentions are likely to be outdated by the time you read this, owing to how fast these tools change. The concepts will be there in different parts of the app if you hunt around.
Wheatfield with Crows
is my favorite Van Gogh painting. It’s stunning in person and
can’t be reproduced
in any medium. Oil paint impasto reflects photons into your eye in ways that aren’t duplicated by ink on paper or by emissive screens. In the same way, the materials and techniques in your existing code and your prompts determine the true qualities of the finished app.
1. Tools Are Not Materials, Nor Technique
Choosing Your Tools
I’m putting this issue here not because it’s the most important but because folks
think
it is. In art, there is a great difference between
tools, materials,
and
technique
. When the work is done, only the materials remain, transformed as they were by your tools and technique.
When you work with AI tools, the materials are your inputs — your code, diagrams, data, and prompts. The technique is how you weave these materials together and the order in which you present them. You’ll find a recurring theme throughout this article: the quality of the materials you provide will be the single most important factor in your AI agent’s success.
My examples will be from
Cursor
but I want to emphasize that the tool
du jour
has very little impact on what you can do, just like all washing machines have similar functions but different buttons.
AI tools change
daily
. If you haven’t updated yours today, it’s probably behind. The trick is to find the tool that offers a workflow that you like — one that offers a balance of investigation and action and boosts your own workflow.
You can apply everything I’ll talk about in Cursor with tools like
Windsurf
,
Copilot
for VS Code, or even by pasting stuff into ChatGPT or Google Gemini. You can also use all of these tools for free but, as with everything in life, the paid version is significantly better, so don’t judge the paid version of something by the free results.
Will non-devs create high quality output with these tools?
Absolutely not.
It’s also important to know your tool deeply and keep up with its
changelog
and documentation. I know no one reads that anymore but, ironically, in the age of “ask an AI anything,” the user of such an AI would do well to read the doc directly as the true secrets of its power are revealed only in the pages of those cryptic tomes.
Know Thyself
When working with AI, you must be realistic about your own abilities and shortcomings, for they will permeate everything the agent builds for you. When is it time to
investigate
, and when is the time to take
action
? You have to be the one to know and control that flow.
With AI tools, different skills pay the bills. Does that mean that non-devs (or non-artists) will create high quality output with these tools?
Absolutely not
. It means just the opposite.
In addition to your standard set of coding skills, you’ll need deep architectural insights and an ability to communicate them in plain English. That’s not a skill set that’s common among programmers. Don’t be upset at the LLM when its output is just as bad as your input.

Forget Me Nots
fame, remi

data.title: Dataframely: A polars-native data frame validation library
data.author: sito42
data.article_summary:
文章主要介绍了QuantCo团队在代码库现代化和数据管道优化过程中遇到的问题及解决方案。他们将数据处理从pandas迁移到polars以提升性能，但发现数据帧的列名、数据类型和值范围等信息不直观，且缺乏运行时验证，导致调试困难和错误难以捕捉。为了解决这一问题，他们评估了pandera和patito等数据帧验证库，但发现这些库在相互依赖的数据帧验证、软验证、测试数据生成和静态类型检查等方面存在不足。

为此，团队开发了dataframely，这是一个专为polars设计的数据帧验证库。dataframely允许开发者定义数据帧模式，并在模式中指定列类型和跨列的验证规则。通过该库，可以确保数据满足预期，提高代码的可读性和健壮性。文章最后展示了如何使用dataframely定义模式和验证数据帧的示例。

Authors
Oliver Borchert
@borchero
Daniel Elsner
@delsner
At QuantCo, we are constantly trying to improve the quality of our code bases to ensure that they remain easily maintainable. More recently, this often involved migrating data pipelines from
pandas
to
polars
in order to achieve significant performance gains.
At the end of 2023, we started undertaking an effort to modernize a massive legacy codebase in our one of our longest-running projects. While doing that, we realized that our existing data frame processing code had an integral flaw: column names, data types, value ranges, and other invariants — none of it was obvious just from reading the code.
As a result, the typical approach for understanding a function's behavior involved executing it on client infrastructure — the only place the actual data is available. Then, we would manually step through each
pandas
transformation to inspect the data before and after every change. Naturally, this is tedious, error-prone, and far from efficient.
Once we'd rewritten a chain of transformations in
polars
, the absence of static type checking or runtime validation on data frame contents meant that bugs were hard to catch. To ensure correctness, we often had to run our entire pipeline end-to-end on large datasets - which required significant time and compute resources.
Eventually, we realized that we needed a better way to describe, validate and reason about the content of the data frames in our data pipeline. We wanted to make invariants obvious while reading the code and actually enforce these invariants at runtime to ensure correctness.
Data frame validation to the rescue
A natural solution to this problem are data frame validation libraries. Already back in 2023, Python libraries existed that allowed defining data frame schemas and verifying that data frames comply with these schemas, i.e. fulfill predefined expectations.
In some projects, we had already been using
pandera
, a widely known open-source library, to validate
pandas
data frames. Unfortunately, back in 2023,
pandera
did not have any
polars
support and a notable polars-native alternative, namely
patito
, was still in its infancy and could not be considered production-ready.
However, even today, we're still encountering several limitations with
pandera
and
patito
for our use case. We concluded that they are inherent to their scope & design and cannot easily be addressed by contributing to these projects - which, we still actively do regardless (e.g., we maintain the conda-forge feedstock of
pandera
).
Specifically,
pandera
and
patito
are missing support for
validation of interdependent data frames
soft validation including introspection of failures
test data generation from schemas
strict static type checking for data frames
Introducing
dataframely
: A polars-native data frame validation library
To remedy the shortcomings of these libraries, we developed
dataframely
.
dataframely
is a declarative data frame validation library with first-class support for
polars
data frames. Its purpose is to make data pipelines written in
polars
(1) more
robust
by ensuring that data meets expectations and (2) more
readable
by adding schema information to data frame type hints.

文章主要介绍了QuantCo团队在代码库现代化和数据管道优化过程中遇到的问题及解决方案。他们将数据处理从pandas迁移到polars以提升性能，但发现数据帧的列名、数据类型和值范围等信息不直观，且缺乏运行时验证，导致调试困难和错误难以捕捉。为了解决这一问题，他们评估了pandera和patito等数据帧验证库，但发现这些库在相互依赖的数据帧验证、软验证、测试数据生成和静态类型检查等方面存在不足。

data.title: Satya Nadella says as much as 30% of Microsoft code is written by software
data.author: shinryudbz
data.article_summary: 微软CEO萨蒂亚·纳德拉透露，该公司目前约有20%-30%的代码由人工智能编写，且这一比例正在稳步上升。他在Meta的首次LlamaCon AI开发者大会上与Meta CEO马克·扎克伯格对话时表示，AI正逐渐替代部分软件开发人员的工作。扎克伯格则提到，Meta正在开发一种AI模型，目标是未来一年内能自动构建一半的AI模型。自OpenAI推出ChatGPT以来，AI已广泛应用于客户服务、软件开发等领域，谷歌、Shopify和Duolingo等公司也在加速采用AI替代人力。这标志着AI在代码编写领域的应用正日益普及。

Key Points
Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella on Tuesday said that as much as 30% of the company's code is now written by artificial intelligence.
Nadella made the comments during a conversation before a live audience with Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg at the social media company's LlamaCon AI developer event.
Zuckerberg said Meta is focused on developing an AI model that can in turn build as much as half of other AI models within the next year.
Facebook's CEO Mark Zuckerberg (L) speaks with Microsoft's CEO Satya Nadella after posing for a family picture with guests who attend the "Tech for Good" Summit at the Elysee Palace in Paris, on May 23, 2018.
Charles Platiau | AFP | Getty Images
Microsoft
CEO Satya Nadella on Tuesday said that as much as 30% of the company's code is now written by artificial intelligence.
"I'd say maybe 20%, 30% of the code that is inside of our repos today and some of our projects are probably all written by software," Nadella said during a conversation before a live audience with
Meta
CEO Mark Zuckerberg.
The pair of CEOs were speaking at Meta's
inaugural LlamaCon
AI developer event in Menlo Park, California. Nadella added that the amount of code being written by AI at Microsoft is going up steadily.
Nadella asked Zuckerberg how much of Meta's code was coming from AI. Zuckerberg said he didn't know the exact figure off the top of his head, but he said Meta is building an AI model that can in turn build future versions of the company's Llama family of AI models.
"Our bet is sort of that in the next year probably … maybe half the development is going to be done by AI, as opposed to people, and then that will just kind of increase from there," Zuckerberg said.
Microsoft and Meta together employ tens of thousands of software developers, but they're the latest companies to discuss how AI is replacing some of the work written by human software developers.
Since OpenAI's launch of ChatGPT in late 2022, people have turned to AI for a number of tasks, including customer service work, generating sales pitches and software development itself.
Google
CEO Sundar Pichai in October said that more than 25% of new code was written by AI. Earlier this month,
Shopify
CEO Tobi Lutke
told employees
that they will have to prove AI cannot do a job before asking for more headcount. Similarly,
Duolingo
CEO Luis von Ahn on Monday
announced in a memo
that the language-teaching company will gradually turn to AI in lieu of human contractors.
Earlier this month CNBC and other outlets reported that OpenAI was in talks to
acquire Windsurf
, a startup with "vibe coding" software that spits out whole programs with a few words of input. The dream is that with machines helping to write code, organizations will be able to produce more and better software.

data.title: The Leaderboard Illusion
data.author: pongogogo
data.article_summary: 文章《The Leaderboard Illusion》讨论了Chatbot Arena排行榜在评估人工智能系统时存在的系统性问题。研究发现，部分供应商通过未公开的私下测试手段，能够在公开发布前测试多种模型变体并选择最佳成绩发布，导致排行榜评分存在选择性披露和偏差。特别是，Meta在Llama-4发布前测试了27种私有模型变体。此外，专有闭源模型在数据获取和保留上具有优势，例如Google和OpenAI获取了大量数据，而开源模型仅获得较少数据。这种不平衡导致了对排行榜特定动态的过度拟合，而非评估模型的整体质量。文章提出了改革建议，以促进更公平、透明的基准测试。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI模型性能测试中的问题和争议

不同观点：
• Simonw认为，资金雄厚的供应商可以提交数十种模型变体，并选择发布表现最好的模型，这种做法让他们拥有巨大优势。他希望知道模型是否经过多次尝试，并建议在公布结果时附带相关信息，如尝试次数和成绩。
• Mrandish指出，由于测试数据可能泄露到训练数据中，以及其他针对测试进行训练的方式，AI模型性能测试结果可能不准确。他认为商业团队为了利益可能会采用各种手段，包括作弊，因此需要对所有测试结果持怀疑态度。
• Godelski强调，测试指标只是指引，不能完全代表模型的真实性能。他引用了Goodhart定律，指出当一个指标成为目标时，它就不再是一个好的指标。他警告不要仅仅依赖指标来评估模型的安全性。

Abstract:
Measuring progress is fundamental to the advancement of any scientific field. As benchmarks play an increasingly central role, they also grow more susceptible to distortion. Chatbot Arena has emerged as the go-to leaderboard for ranking the most capable AI systems. Yet, in this work we identify systematic issues that have resulted in a distorted playing field. We find that undisclosed private testing practices benefit a handful of providers who are able to test multiple variants before public release and retract scores if desired. We establish that the ability of these providers to choose the best score leads to biased Arena scores due to selective disclosure of performance results. At an extreme, we identify 27 private LLM variants tested by Meta in the lead-up to the Llama-4 release. We also establish that proprietary closed models are sampled at higher rates (number of battles) and have fewer models removed from the arena than open-weight and open-source alternatives. Both these policies lead to large data access asymmetries over time. Providers like Google and OpenAI have received an estimated 19.2% and 20.4% of all data on the arena, respectively. In contrast, a combined 83 open-weight models have only received an estimated 29.7% of the total data. We show that access to Chatbot Arena data yields substantial benefits; even limited additional data can result in relative performance gains of up to 112% on the arena distribution, based on our conservative estimates. Together, these dynamics result in overfitting to Arena-specific dynamics rather than general model quality. The Arena builds on the substantial efforts of both the organizers and an open community that maintains this valuable evaluation platform. We offer actionable recommendations to reform the Chatbot Arena's evaluation framework and promote fairer, more transparent benchmarking for the field

43842380.article_summary: 文章《The Leaderboard Illusion》讨论了Chatbot Arena排行榜在评估人工智能系统时存在的系统性问题。研究发现，部分供应商通过未公开的私下测试手段，能够在公开发布前测试多种模型变体并选择最佳成绩发布，导致排行榜评分存在选择性披露和偏差。特别是，Meta在Llama-4发布前测试了27种私有模型变体。此外，专有闭源模型在数据获取和保留上具有优势，例如Google和OpenAI获取了大量数据，而开源模型仅获得较少数据。这种不平衡导致了对排行榜特定动态的过度拟合，而非评估模型的整体质量。文章提出了改革建议，以促进更公平、透明的基准测试。

Unlocking the Reasoning Potential of Language Model
From Pretraining to Posttraining
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Apache2.0 License
.
I. Introduction
Currently, most successful RL works, including open-source research, rely on relatively large base models, e.g., 32B models, particularly for enhancing code reasoning capabilities. Moreover, it was widely considered that achieving uniform and simultaneous improvements in both mathematical and code capabilities within a small model is challenging. Nonetheless, we believe that the effectiveness of the RL trained reasoning model relies on the inherent reasoning potential of the base model. To fully unlock the reasoning potential of language models, efforts must focus not only on post-training but also on pre-training strategies tailored to reasoning.
In this work, we present MiMo-7B, a series of models trained from scratch and born for reasoning tasks. Our RL experiments from MiMo-7B-Base show that our model possesses extraordinary reasoning potential, even surpassing much larger 32B models. Additionally, we perform RL training on a cold-started SFT model, resulting in MiMo-7B-RL, which demonstrates superior performance on both mathematics and code reasoning tasks, matching the performance of OpenAI o1-mini.
We open-source MiMo-7B series, including checkpoints of the base model, SFT model, RL model trained from base model, and RL model trained from the SFT model.
We believe this report along with the models will provides valuable insights to develop powerful reasoning LLM that benefit the larger community.
🌟 Highlights
Pre-Training: Base Model Born for Reasoning
We optimize data preprocessing pipeline, enhancing text extraction toolkits and applying multi-dimensional data filtering to increase reasoning pattern density in pre-training data. We also employ multiple strategies to generate massive diverse synthetic reasoning data.
We adopt a three-stage data mixture strategy for pre-training. Overall, MiMo-7B-Base is pre-trained on approximately 25 trillion tokens.
We incorporate Multiple-Token Prediction as an additional training objective, which enhances model performance and accelerates inference.
Post-Training Recipe: Pioneering Reasoning Model
We curate 130K mathematics and code problems as RL training data, which can be verified by rule-based verifiers. Each problem undergoes careful cleaning and difficulty assessment to ensure quality. We employ only rule-based accuracy rewards to avoid potential reward hacking.
To mitigate the sparse reward issue for challenging code problems, we introduce a test difficulty driven code reward. By assigning fine-grained scores for test cases with varying difficulty levels, the policy can be more effectively optimized via dense reward signal.
We implement a data re-sampling strategy for easy problems to enhance rollout sampling efficiency and stabilize policy updates, particularly in the later phases of RL training.
RL Infrastructures
We develop a Seamless Rollout Engine to accelerate RL training and validation. Our design integrates continuous rollout, asynchronous reward computation, and early termination to minimize GPU idle time, achieving 2.29$\times$ faster training and 1.96$\times$ faster validation.
We support MTP in vLLM and enhance the robustness of the inference engine in RL system.

• **Havoc的观点**：过去的新型加密货币至少试图假装包含某种金融创新，而现在都是名人代言、炒作和谎言。特别是美国总统在任期间参与加密货币活动让人感到震惊。

• **bgwalter的观点**：提到一个公开的募资活动，并询问关于比特币基金救助骗局是否仍然存在，或者比特币是否已经表现良好到不需要救助。

• **revel的观点**：曾对加密货币充满信心并创立相关公司，但由于行业方向令人失望而离开。担心政府在法律和监管上的不作为，而现在特朗普币成为裸的贿赂和腐败工具，强调需要一定程度的监管。

• **instagib的观点**：提到公司规则不允许特朗普等人出售他们的币，但可能会在其他买家同意的情况下解除限制，表示对这种说法持怀疑态度。

• **techterrier的观点**：推测支持特朗普的Web 3.0群体可能预见到了这种情况。

• **hypeatei的观点**：指出现在不再有人提到“沼泽”，因为有一个现任总统正在进行加密货币诈骗。对特朗普相关行为缺乏阴谋论讨论表示不满。

• **WinstonSmith84的观点**：作为加密货币爱好者，认为特朗普让这个行业看起来很糟糕，并担心加密货币与特朗普联系在一起。指出缺乏监管使得这些骗局没有受到任何惩罚。

• **VeejayRampay的观点**：从欧洲角度看，这种行为类似于盗贼统治，在2025年仍然可能存在，感到荒谬。

• **whyage的观点**：询问可以采取什么措施来制止这种明目张胆的欺诈行为。

• **bediger4000的观点**：认为这篇文章在淡化腐败，并确认特朗普通过其加密货币操作接受贿赂。

• **yalogin的观点**：对其支持者忽视的腐败和无能程度感到震惊，认为这一切都是因为他们不喜欢移民。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于加密货币行业是否需要更多监管，以及名人特别是政治人物参与加密货币活动是否导致腐败和欺诈。
- 不同评论者对特朗普及其相关加密货币活动的道德和法律问题表达了强烈不满。
- 一些评论者对加密货币行业的未来表示担忧，认为当前的状况损害了行业的声誉和可信度。

主要讨论点：氟化水政策的合理性及个人选择权

不同观点：
• delichon：支持佛罗里达州允许居民选择是否接受氟化水处理，基于个人对身体自主权的考虑。作为甲状腺癌幸存者，他认为氟化物会影响碘的吸收，从而导致健康问题。他将这一立场与支持堕胎选择权相比较，强调个人选择权。
• jemmyw：认为人们对氟化水话题反应过度，添加的氟化物剂量很低，且经过充分研究。他提到某些地区需要去除自然产生的氟化物，并指出新西兰正朝强制添加氟化物的方向发展。
• Etheryte：指出全球对氟化水没有共识，如多数欧盟国家选择在牙膏或食盐中添加氟化物，而非水中。
• os2warpman：以讽刺语气表达对“强制用药”的不满，暗示未来可能会禁止在盐中加碘或牛奶中加维生素D。
• ifyoubuildit：批评评论中出现的反感情绪，认为有些问题比氟化水更值得关注，并指出讨论中的保守倾向。
• peterpost2：对美国当前状况表示困惑和担忧。
• amazingamazing：强调局部使用氟化物（如牙膏）比饮用氟化水更有效，并批评在事实面前仍有人持否定态度。
• esbranson：指出贫困人群由于对媒体的不信任而不喝自来水，并将这一现象归因于更广泛的社会问题，建议削减公共广播公司资金以防止“愚蠢”蔓延。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于个人是否有权选择是否接受氟化水处理，以及氟化水政策的科学依据和实际效果。

• 不同国家和地区对氟化物的处理方式也被提及，显示出全球对此问题缺乏一致意见。
