But overall, the time savings from using AI was less than expected. According to the study, "users report average time savings of just 2.8 percent of work hours" from using AI tools. That's a bit more than one hour per 40 hour work week.
The authors note that this finding differs from other randomized controlled trials that have found productivity benefits on the order of
15 percent
. And they explain this discrepancy by saying that other studies have focused on occupations with high AI productivity potential and that real-world workers don't operate under the same conditions.
"So I think there are two key reasons why the real economic gains are lower than [the cited studies]," said Humlum, noting that his study relies on actual tax data.
"First, most tasks do not fall into that category where ChatGPT can just automate everything. And then second, we're in

data.author: matt_d
data.article_summary:
这篇文章介绍了Haskell中对"packed data"格式的支持，旨在简化数据序列化与反序列化过程。通常，程序在持久化数据或通过网络传输数据时需要序列化，而接收数据时需要反序列化，这些步骤会消耗时间和增加数据大小。文章提出了一种"packed"数据格式，允许数据以二进制格式直接使用，无需反序列化，从而提升性能，尤其是在处理树结构时，因无需指针跳转，能更有效利用L1缓存。

文章提到的`packed-data`库通过Haskell的类型系统和模板元编程（Template Haskell）实现了数据打包、解包及遍历功能，而无需修改编译器。该库提供了`Packable`和`Unpackable`类型类用于打包与解包，并支持自定义的模式匹配函数。文章还介绍了`NeedsBuilder`类型，用于构建打包数据，灵感来源于"Linear Haskell"论文中的类型设计。尽管目前packed data主要用于研究项目，但`packed-data`库提供了一种在Haskell中本地支持packed data的创新方法。

• tlb 则质疑了序列化数据比内存中表示更大的观点，认为二进制序列化数据通常不会比内存表示更大。他指出，像map这样的数据类型为了支持快速查找和可变性，在内存中通常会更大。

Packed Data support in Haskell
Contents
Packed Data support in Haskell
This blog post aims to be a short and accessible summary of a paper that will be published at ECOOP 2025, titled
Type-safe and portable support for packed data
(Link of the pre-print version
here
).
Introduction: Packed Data
When programs want to persist data or send it over the network, they need to
serialise
it (e.g. to JSON or XML). On the other hand, when a program receives data from the network or reads it from a file, data needs to be
deserialised
.
flowchart LR
Server(["Server"])
Server --> SD["Serialise"]
SD -- Network --- RD["Deserialise"]
RD --> Client(["Client"])
These de/serialisation steps are necessary because
we cannot use the in-memory representation/layout of the data in a file or when sending it over the network
, mainly because of the pointers it may contain.
Consequently,
de/serialising data has a cost
: it takes time, and the serialised version of the data is usually bigger than its in-memory representation. In the context of systems that interact through the network, it leads to
larger payloads
to send, and thus
slower transfer times
.
Now,
what if we didn’t have to serialise the data before sending it to a client
, and
what if the client could use the data from the network as-is
, without any marshalling steps? We could save some time, on both the server and client side.
Introducing the
‘packed’ data format
, a binary format that allows using data as it is, without the need for a deserialisation step. A notable perk of this format is that
traversals on packed trees is proven to be faster than on ‘unpacked’ trees
: as the fields of data structures are inlines, there are no pointer jumps, thus making the most of the L1 cache.
To better understand how it looks like, here is a representation of a tree in memory that uses pointers.
N
represents nodes, and
L
represents leaves. Numbers are the tree’s data, and dots and arrows are pointers.
Pointer-based tree layout in memory
Here is what a packed tree looks like in memory.
Packed tree layout in memory
A few projects use or leverage this ‘packed’ approach. For example, Cap’n Proto
1
is a popular library that allows packing data (i.e. build a binary buffer containing the data), using that buffer as-is (e.g. traverse it and ‘unpack’ fields of a structure). However, no languages support packed data natively. Haskell does support compact normal forms (CNF), but the
Compact
data type does not allow using (e.g. deconstructing) packed values. We should note the existence of
Gibbon
, a research compiler that accepts functional programs and generates programs that use packed data natively.
Unfortunately
the use of packed data is limited to research projects
, probably because it’s kinda hard to support it.
In this post, I will introduce
the
packed-data
Haskell library
. It
allows packing and unpacking data, as well as traversing packed data as-is
(with a custom
case
function), with no marshalling step or compiler mods, thanks to the power of types. As far as we are aware, this is on of the first effort to bring support for packed data using only the host language’s type-system, meta-programming (Template Haskell)
with no compiler modifications
.
The library, its features and its API
Using Template Haskell,
packed-data
generates all the necessary code so that one can, for
any
type
2

pack
data (i.e. serialise the data into a binary format)
unpack
data (i.e. deserialise the data from that binary format)
traverse
the data, thanks to a generated
case
function that allows pattern matching on a data type’s constructor.

• lordleft 对文章本身表示赞赏，但没有对具体技术细节做出评价。

• NetOpWibby 将“packed”数据格式类比为Haskell的MessagePack，暗示这可能是一种新的序列化方式。

• gitroom 表示支持这种“packed”格式，认为减少内存操作总是有益的，能提高效率。

补充讨论：
• nine_k 的评论中提到了“packed”格式在缓存利用和网络传输方面的优势，强调了其零拷贝内存读取的特点。
• tlb 的评论引发了关于序列化数据大小与内存表示大小的争议，特别是针对不同数据类型和序列化方式。
• NetOpWibby 的评论指出了“packed”格式与其他序列化格式（如MessagePack）的相似性，可能引起对不同格式适用场景的进一步讨论。
• gitroom 强调了减少内存操作步骤对性能提升的重要性，支持采用这种新的数据格式。

争议焦点：序列化数据是否通常比内存中表示更大，特别是在二进制序列化的情况下。tlb 对此持怀疑态度，而 nine_k 则强调了“packed”格式在特定场景下的优势。

data.author: tennysont
data.article_summary:
文章介绍了对非传统计算形式的新兴趣，尤其是在“摩尔定律已死”的担忧下。这些形式包括量子计算、模拟计算和可逆计算等。可逆计算被认为是最节能的方式，基于Landauer原理，其理论能耗远低于当前技术水平。文章通过AMD Ryzen处理器的例子说明现有计算设备的效率比理论最大值低约9个数量级。

文章详细介绍了一种使用连杆和旋转关节构建图灵完备机械计算系统的方法，核心组件包括“锁”、“平衡”和“曲柄”。这些组件可以实现NAND门，从而构建任何逻辑电路。文章最后提到Ralph Merkle等人对这种机械计算的详细介绍，并感谢Haochen Xu对演示界面的改进。

总之，尽管现有技术距离理论最大效率还有很大差距，但探索不同计算范式既有趣又具有前瞻性。

• 参与者不仅讨论了理论，还分享了实际操作经验和具体例子，提供了技术讨论的实践背景。

Mechanical Computing
Intro
With the concern that “Moore’s Law is dead,” new interest has grown for unconventional forms of computing. This includes:
quantum computing
(for atomic simulations and specific NP approximation algorithms)
analog computing
(for fast-and-efficient-but-error-prone computation, such as neural net inference)
reversible computing
(for maximum energy efficiency)
It is believed that the most efficient computing devices would use little or no entropy during reversible computations, and only consume energy during non-reversible parts of computation. Specifically, the
Landauer’s principle
states that all non-physically-reversible computation operations consume at least \(2.9 \times 10^{21}\) J of energy at room temperature (and less as the temperature drops).
Are we at the theoretical maximum efficiency yet? No. Using some back-of-the-napkin math:
AMD Ryzen Threadripper 7995WX has about 12 TFLOPS of FP32 (single-precision) compute (
link
)
Assuming 30 irreversible computations per FP32 operation (from Claude), we have 10
14.5
irreversible computations per second
At 350 W this is about \(10^{-12}\) J per irreversible computation, or about
9 orders of magnitude
less efficient than the theoretical maximum
Even if a CPU like the AMD Ryzen Z1 Extreme or Apple M4 can improve this efficiency by a factor of 10 (which is too generous), we’re still a long way out from hitting the theoretical wall.
Nevertheless, it is both fun and prudent to imagine how different paradigms of computing would work. These different paradigms might even be competitive in certain niches long before transistors hit a wall. My favorite reversible computing scheme comes from a paper named
Mechanical Computing Systems Using Only Links and Rotary Joint
. In it, they use
links
and
rotary joints
(hinges) to build Turing-complete computing machines.
The “Lock”
The most basic element is a “lock.” It’s constructed with two triangles that are allowed to slide back and forth. However, once the top triangle has been pushed forward, it prevents the bottom triangle from being pushed forward (and vice versa). It’s called a “lock” because the first triangle to get pushed forward will “lock out” the other.
The demo below is made from springs and pivot points. Drag the sliders to engage the top and bottom parts of a lock.
Top Input:
Bottom Input:
In principle, these locks could be constructed out of physical materials on very small scales. The authors of the original paper provided this example schematic of a 30 x 30 x 7 nm lock constructed out of carbon:
The “Balance”
Ultimately, our binary convention will be that either the “1” line or the “0” line of a bit will always be engaged. A balance helps make this happen. It consists of two locks and a lever before them. On the forward edge of a clock, it forces a horizontal translation through whichever lock is not already engaged.
Try engaging only one of the two locks (top or bottom) and then engaging the clock. The clock will “flow through” whichever lock has not already been engaged by the inputs:
Top Input:
Bottom Input:
Clock Input:
Bellcrank
The last thing that we will need to construct a NAND gate is a way to route and split signals. It turns out to be relatively simple:
Input:
NAND Simulation
And now we are ready to construct a NAND gate, which is a “universal gate” (i.e., you can implement any truth table using only NAND gates). We first use two “wires” for each input. If
A
is
TRUE
, then the first wire is pushed forward. If
A
is
FALSE
, then the second wire is pushed forward. Likewise, if
B
is
TRUE
then the third wire is pushed forward, and the fourth wire is pushed forward if
B
is
FALSE
.
We expect to always have exactly two of these wires push forward for any computation. Following these input wires, we see that each individual wire engages exactly two locks, preventing the thrust of the clock from flowing through that pathway. Since there are four pathways, we must make sure that only one pathway is unlocked at any time. Then, when the clock arrives, that pathway will receive the forward thrust.

Ralph Merkle: Molecular Mechanical Computing
.
Acknowledgement
This was inspired by the paper
Mechanical Computing Systems Using Only Links and Rotary Joint
(Ralph C. Merkle, Robert A. Freitas Jr., Tad Hogg, Thomas E. Moore, Matthew S. Moses, James Ryley). And a big thanks to

data.article_summary: OpenPipe ART是一个开源的强化学习训练库，旨在通过最小代码改动提升大型语言模型（LLM）在代理工作流中的表现。它采用GRPO强化学习算法，支持在现有代码库中执行代理运行，同时将复杂的强化学习训练循环交由ART后端处理。ART功能分为客户端和服务器，客户端负责与代码库交互，服务器独立运行进行模型训练。训练过程包括推断、奖励分配和模型更新，循环执行直到达到指定迭代次数。目前ART支持大多数vLLM/HuggingFace兼容的因果语言模型，但Gemma 3暂不支持。ART仍处于alpha阶段，欢迎贡献和反馈。

Train GRPO-powered RL agents with minimal code changes and maximal performance!
Agent Reinforcement Trainer (ART)
ART is an open-source reinforcement training library for improving LLM performance in agentic workflows. ART utilizes the powerful GRPO reinforcement learning algorithm to train models from their own experiences. Unlike most RL libraries, ART allows you to execute agent runs
in your existing codebase
while offloading all the complexity of the RL training loop to the ART backend. Read about the
training loop
. Then try out one of the notebooks below!
📒 Notebooks
Agent Task
Example Notebook
Description
Comparative Performance

benchmarks

Qwen 2.5 7B learns to solve Temporal Clue
[Link coming soon]

Qwen 2.5 3B learns to play Tic Tac Toe
benchmarks
🔁 Training Loop Overview
ART's functionality is divided into a
client
and a
server
. The OpenAI-compatible client is responsible for interfacing between ART and your codebase. Using the client, you can pass messages and get completions from your LLM as it improves. The server runs independently on any machine with a GPU. It abstracts away the complexity of the inference and training portions of the RL loop while allowing for some custom configuration. An outline of the training loop is shown below:
Inference
Your code uses the ART client to perform an agentic workflow (usually executing several rollouts in parallel to gather data faster).
Completion requests are routed to the ART server, which runs the model's latest LoRA in vLLM.
As the agent executes, each
system
,
user
, and
assistant
message is stored in a Trajectory.
When a rollout finishes, your code assigns a
reward
to its Trajectory, indicating the performance of the LLM.
Training
When each rollout has finished, Trajectories are grouped and sent to the server. Inference is blocked while training executes.
The server trains your model using GRPO, initializing from the latest checkpoint (or an empty LoRA on the first iteration).
The server saves the newly trained LoRA to a local directory and loads it into vLLM.
Inference is unblocked and the loop resumes at step 1.
This training loop runs until a specified number of inference and training iterations have completed.
Supported Models
ART should work with most vLLM/HuggingFace-transformers compatible causal language models, or at least the ones supported by
Unsloth
. Gemma 3 does not appear to be supported for the time being. If any other model isn't working for you, please let us know on
Discord
or open an issue on
GitHub
!
⚠️
Disclaimer
ART is currently in alpha and has only been tested on a few projects in the wild! We're working hard to make it work for everyone, but if you run into any issues, please let us know on
Discord
or open an issue on
GitHub
!
🤝 Contributing
ART is in very active development, and contributions are most welcome! Please see the
CONTRIBUTING.md
file for more information.
🙏 Credits
ART stands on the shoulders of giants. While we owe many of the ideas and early experiments that led to ART's development to the open source RL community at large, we're especially grateful to the authors of the following projects:
Unsloth
vLLM
trl
SkyPilot
Finally, thank you to our partners who've helped us test ART in the wild! We're excited to see what you all build with it.

data.article_summary: DeepSeek-Prover-V2是一款开源的大语言模型，专为Lean 4中的形式化定理证明设计。该模型通过DeepSeek-V3的递归定理证明管道收集初始数据，利用7B模型处理每个子目标的证明搜索，以减少计算负担。在合成冷启动数据后，通过强化学习进一步提升模型能力，最终在神经定理证明中达到了顶尖性能，miniF2F测试集上的通过率达88.9%。此外，文章还介绍了包含325个问题的ProverBench基准数据集，涵盖从高中竞赛到本科水平的数学问题。DeepSeek-Prover-V2提供7B和671B参数两个版本，可从HuggingFace下载。

DeepSeek-Prover-V2: Advancing Formal Mathematical Reasoning via Reinforcement Learning for Subgoal Decomposition
1. Introduction
We introduce DeepSeek-Prover-V2, an open-source large language model designed for formal theorem proving in Lean 4, with initialization data collected through a recursive theorem proving pipeline powered by DeepSeek-V3. The cold-start training procedure begins by prompting DeepSeek-V3 to decompose complex problems into a series of subgoals. The proofs of resolved subgoals are synthesized into a chain-of-thought process, combined with DeepSeek-V3's step-by-step reasoning, to create an initial cold start for reinforcement learning. This process enables us to integrate both informal and formal mathematical reasoning into a unified model.
2. Model Summary
Synthesize Cold-Start Reasoning Data through Recursive Proof Search
To construct the cold-start dataset, we develop a simple yet effective pipeline for recursive theorem proving, utilizing DeepSeek-V3 as a unified tool for both subgoal decomposition and formalization. We prompt DeepSeek-V3 to decompose theorems into high-level proof sketches while simultaneously formalizing these proof steps in Lean 4, resulting in a sequence of subgoals.
We use a smaller 7B model to handle the proof search for each subgoal, thereby reducing the associated computational burden. Once the decomposed steps of a challenging problem are resolved, we pair the complete step-by-step formal proof with the corresponding chain-of-thought from DeepSeek-V3 to create cold-start reasoning data.
Reinforcement Learning with Synthetic Cold-Start Data
We curate a subset of challenging problems that remain unsolved by the 7B prover model in an end-to-end manner, but for which all decomposed subgoals have been successfully resolved. By composing the proofs of all subgoals, we construct a complete formal proof for the original problem. This proof is then appended to DeepSeek-V3's chain-of-thought, which outlines the corresponding lemma decomposition, thereby producing a cohesive synthesis of informal reasoning and subsequent formalization.
After fine-tuning the prover model on the synthetic cold-start data, we perform a reinforcement learning stage to further enhance its ability to bridge informal reasoning with formal proof construction. Following the standard training objective for reasoning models, we use binary correct-or-incorrect feedback as the primary form of reward supervision.
The resulting model, DeepSeek-Prover-V2-671B, achieves state-of-the-art performance in neural theorem proving, reaching
$88.9$
% pass ratio on the MiniF2F-test and solving 49 out of 658 problems from PutnamBench. The proofs generated by DeepSeek-Prover-V2 for the miniF2F dataset are available for download as a
ZIP archive
.
3. ProverBench: Formalization of AIME and Textbook Problems
we introduce ProverBench, a benchmark dataset comprising 325 problems. Of these, 15 are formalized from number theory and algebra questions featured in the recent AIME competitions (AIME 24 and 25), offering authentic high-school competition-level challenges. The remaining 310 problems are drawn from curated textbook examples and educational tutorials, contributing a diverse and pedagogically grounded collection of formalized mathematical problems. This benchmark is designed to enable more comprehensive evaluation across both high-school competition problems and undergraduate-level mathematics.

We release DeepSeek-Prover-V2 in two model sizes: 7B and 671B parameters. DeepSeek-Prover-V2-671B is trained on top of DeepSeek-V3-Base. DeepSeek-Prover-V2-7B is built upon DeepSeek-Prover-V1.5-Base and features an extended context length of up to 32K tokens.

data.title: NotebookLM Audio Overviews are now available in over 50 languages
data.author: saikatsg
data.article_summary: Google Labs宣布NotebookLM的音频概述功能现支持超过50种语言。该功能将资料转化为类似播客的对话，去年一经推出便广受欢迎。现在，借助Gemini的原生音频支持，用户可以用自己偏好的语言生成音频概述，包括南非荷兰语、印地语、土耳其语等。音频概述将根据用户账户的默认语言生成，且新增的“输出语言”选项允许随时更改语言，方便创建多语言内容或学习资料。例如，教师可以为学生提供多种语言的资源，学生可根据需要生成相应语言的音频概述。此功能旨在打破语言障碍，让信息更加 accessible。用户可访问notebooklm.google体验。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：NotebookLM的音频概述/播客功能及其使用体验

不同观点：
• ljoshua：认为NotebookLM的音频功能对家庭学校的孩子非常有帮助。他们的孩子通过听音频学习，然后与家长一起讨论和进行相关活动，提高了学习效率。
• mikeocool：批评NotebookLM播客过于夸张，尤其是在语言和叙述风格上，一个主持人会不断重复另一个主持人的话，显得非常冗余。
• tkgally：尝试了日语版本，认为总体不错，但在处理日语特有的回话（如 aizuchi）时有些不自然，但整体效果仍然可以接受。
• ipsum2：认为NotebookLM对转换论文为播客的用途不够实用，解释过于笼统，且包含过多不重要的内容，怀疑使用更高级的模型（如Gemini 2.5 Pro）可能会改善效果。
• qwertox：上传了一个Python脚本，生成的播客对非技术人员理解其工作内容有帮助。
• chupchap：使用NotebookLM进行度假规划，生成的播客效果不错，并且增加了趣味性。
• ksynwa：询问是否有便宜或免费的服务可以将英文文章转换为音频文件，并表示不需要播客或对话形式。
• TekMol：不喜欢播客风格的音频，希望能有一个直接阅读文本而不加修饰的选项。
• lenwood：总体喜欢NotebookLM的播客功能，但不喜欢主持人频繁接话和完成对方句子的情况，认为这很分散注意力。
• hu3：喜欢将Hacker News评论生成播客，认为有助于快速了解讨论的总体情况。
• Almondsetat：不理解为什么选择播客风格，认为这种形式初次体验可能印象深刻，但很快会变得令人厌烦，特别是在主持人对话内容忽深忽浅时。
• ahmedfromtunis：最喜欢可以与“主持人”互动以获取澄清或引导讨论重点的功能，即使这些内容在原始材料中没有涉及。
• ccbikai：认为中文语音效果不如Minimax，并提供Hacker Podcast进行比较。
• davidg707：创建了一个基于自己博客文章的播客，父母 initially 误以为他取得了很大成就，知道真相后既有些失望又有些惊讶。
• tinyhouse：质疑NotebookLM没有应用程序的问题。

补充讨论：
• NotebookLM的音频功能在不同语言和文化背景下的表现存在差异，比如日语中的回话处理问题。
• 用户对播客风格的接受度存在分歧，有些人喜欢其互动性和趣味性，而另一些人则觉得对话过于夸张和分散注意力。
• 用户对模型和生成内容的质量有不同期待，有些人希望能有更高级的模型选择和更简洁的内容呈现方式。
• 对于是否需要应用程序，部分用户表达了对NotebookLM缺乏移动端支持的疑惑。

Audio Overviews are now multilingual, and you can try it out today.
Michael Chen
Software Engineer, Google Labs
Arielle Fox
Program Manager, Google Labs
Share

Copy link
Last year, we expanded NotebookLM to more than 200 countries and now we’re making Audio Overviews available in more than 50 languages.
Audio Overviews
, which turn your sources into engaging, podcast-like conversations, were immediately popular when they launched late last year. Now, thanks to Gemini’s native audio support, even more people can use Audio Overviews in their preferred language, from
Afrikaans to Hindi to Turkish — and more.
This is an early look at what's possible with this feature — we plan to keep building and refining it based on your feedback.
Audio Overviews are generated in your account’s preferred language. This update also introduces a new "Output Language" option in NotebookLM's settings; your Audio Overviews are always generated in the language you select here. You can change the language at any time and your audio and chat responses will reflect this, making it easy to create multilingual content or study materials as needed.
For example, a teacher preparing a lesson on the Amazon rainforest can share resources in various languages — like a Portuguese documentary, a Spanish research paper and English study reports — with their students. The students can upload these and can generate an Audio Overview of key insights in their preferred language. This capability breaks down language barriers and makes the information more accessible to everyone.
We hope bringing more languages to Audio Overviews helps you discover new insights and connect with information in your own language. Try it out today at
notebooklm.google
. Give it a listen, 來聽看看, écoutez!

• TekMol：不喜欢播客风格的音频，希望能有一个直接阅读文本而不加修饰的选项。
• lenwood：总体喜欢NotebookLM的播客功能，但不喜欢主持人频繁接话和完成对方句子的情况，认为这很分散注意力。
• hu3：喜欢将Hacker News评论生成播客，认为有助于快速了解讨论的总体情况。
• Almondsetat：不理解为什么选择播客风格，认为这种形式初次体验可能印象深刻，但很快会变得令人厌烦，特别是在主持人对话内容忽深忽浅时。
• ahmedfromtunis：最喜欢可以与“主持人”互动以获取澄清或引导讨论重点的功能，即使这些内容在原始材料中没有涉及。
• ccbikai：认为中文语音效果不如Minimax，并提供Hacker Podcast进行比较。
• davidg707：创建了一个基于自己博客文章的播客，父母 initially 误以为他取得了很大成就，知道真相后既有些失望又有些惊讶。
• tinyhouse：质疑NotebookLM没有应用程序的问题。

补充讨论：
• NotebookLM的音频功能在不同语言和文化背景下的表现存在差异，比如日语中的回话处理问题。
• 用户对播客风格的接受度存在分歧，有些人喜欢其互动性和趣味性，而另一些人则觉得对话过于夸张和分散注意力。
• 用户对模型和生成内容的质量有不同期待，有些人希望能有更高级的模型选择和更简洁的内容呈现方式。
• 对于是否需要应用程序，部分用户表达了对NotebookLM缺乏移动端支持的疑惑。

data.title: Show HN: Create your own finetuned AI model using Google Sheets
data.author: QueensGambit
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一系列增强和扩展Google Forms功能的产品及服务。包括通过AI自动填写表单、定制用户界面、上传文件、分配分数、发送邮件通知、收集电子签名、确保HIPAA合规等。此外，还提到了一款基于Google Sheets的AI模型构建工具，允许用户无需编码即可创建和优化AI模型，支持多种AI引擎并提供API集成和版本控制功能。这些工具旨在简化流程、提高效率，并适用于各种行业需求。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕PromptRepo服务的有效性、定价、技术复杂性及目标用户的讨论。

不同观点：
• Centigonal：认为大多数客户通过简单的策略（如提示、工作流设计、RAG等）就能获得显著改进，只有少数客户需要进行精细调整（fine-tuning）。随着AI技术的发展，这一情况可能会改变。
• rgbrgb：指出市场竞争激烈，认可PromptRepo的UI设计，但表示由于时间和成本问题，不会成为早期采用者。建议通过API密钥或积分系统来降低成本。
• ygreif：对现代fine-tuning技术不太了解，质疑其技术复杂性，如改变多少层、学习率等是否应该对用户可见，以及实际需要多少样本。
• raylad：质疑PromptRepo的目标客户，认为网站描述不够清晰，建议提供更详细的应用示例。
• scosman：对选择以电子表格为核心表示疑问，认为大多数人缺乏数据集，需要帮助构建。分享了自己在构建自定义UI的经验。
• ipaddr：不喜欢定价策略，认为年付费方式和价格翻倍让人不满。
• heresjohnny：建议不应将自带选项（BYO）作为单独的轻量包，认为定价页面对非技术人员不够友好。但认可服务的价值，认为销售和营销人员可能是首批用户。
• ricktdotorg：对服务表示兴趣，分享了自己使用Google Sheet构建客户支持聊天机器人的经验，并表示会进行研究。
• nbbaier：报告访问PromptRepo网站时遇到连接错误。
• justanotheratom：指出fine-tuning操作平台需要对比不同模型的评估、延迟和成本。
• gitroom：对工具简化表示赞赏，但质疑简单界面是否真的帮助用户获得更好结果，还是仅仅让更多人尝试。
• labrador：质疑PromptRepo与OpenAI项目的区别。
• littlestymaar：质疑使用Google Sheet让客户将训练数据提供给Google。
• ivape：尽管目前没有fine-tuning的需求，但认为使用电子表格是最简单的解决方案。
• mogili：认为PromptRepo本质上是将CSV文件转换为JSONL并传递给fine-tuning服务的自动化前端。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于服务的定价和目标用户定位不明确，部分用户对技术复杂性和实际需求存在疑问。
• 用户对电子表格集成方式的便利性表示认可，但也有人对其涉及的数据隐私问题表示担忧。
• 部分用户对市场竞争和工具的实际效果持观望态度，认为需要更多示例和应用场景来证明其价值。

data.title: Someone at YouTube needs glasses
data.author: jaydenmilne
data.article_summary: 这篇文章表达了对YouTube界面变化的不满。作者在32寸1440p显示器上打开YouTube时，只看到五个视频，且页面很大一部分将被巨幅广告占据。相比之下，2019年1月的YouTube页面能显示30个视频，且没有广告。作者对这种界面调整（可能是A/B测试）感到失望，并幽默地预测到2026年5月YouTube主页可能仅展示一个视频，到2026年9月可能完全没有视频。文章最后怀念了过去没有过多商业化的YouTube，认为其越来越注重盈利，失去了原有的用户体验。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：YouTube主页视频网格布局及其用户体验问题

不同观点：
• **rozab** 认为视频网格排列不齐，且自动播放功能令人困扰。自动播放隐藏了精心设计的缩略图，且有时视频会无故添加到观看历史中。
• **herpdyderp** 提供了一种技术解决方案，通过uBlock Origin插件调整视频网格布局，修复了对齐问题。
• **Starlevel004** 提到视频数量从12个减少，搜索结果中插入不相关的推荐视频，损害了用户体验。
• **InMice** 支持rozab的观点，并提到安装"Control Panel for Youtube"插件可以解决问题，同时也能够将短视频恢复为传统播放器播放。
• **voytec** 提供了一种通过RSS订阅YouTube频道的方法，以避免网站上的干扰。
• **_QrE** 表示通过关闭历史记录功能，可以避免个性化推荐，并认为这种做法使YouTube使用更加慎重。
• **dcchambers** 强烈希望能够永久禁用YouTube Shorts，因为尽管选择了“少显示此类内容”，这些短视频仍然出现在显眼位置。
• **schainks** 选择关闭推荐视频功能，只观看订阅频道或他人分享的视频，认为这样可以避免浪费时间在“发现”功能上。
• **iMerNibor** 指出缩略图被拉伸导致模糊的问题，并质疑这种问题如何通过质量检测。
• **insin** 开发了一个浏览器插件，允许用户自定义视频数量和间距，并能完全隐藏Shorts，提供了更多选项和功能来改善YouTube体验。
• **Havoc** 提到点击缩略图时被引导至帮助页面的问题，质疑YouTube的UI设计是否合理。
• **cpersona** 指出YouTube在不登录情况下不再显示视频，支持了评论中关于页面变化的观点。
• **meltyness** 认为YouTube通过降低长视频内容的可用性和质量，来重新集中活动于短视频内容，反映了“增长后期”的策略问题。
• **vinnymac** 分享了在iOS应用上的不佳体验，展示了一个截图作为例子。
• **II2II** 提到在隐私模式下，视频被“尝试搜索以开始”的消息取代，并认为这种变化已经提前实现。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点主要集中在YouTube自动播放功能、视频缩略图设计及其对用户体验的影响。
• 用户对YouTube Shorts的强制显示表示不满，并希望有更好的控制选项。
• 技术解决方案和插件的使用成为用户应对不良设计的主要手段。
• 部分用户选择关闭个性化推荐和历史记录功能，以避免干扰，并认为这种方法提高了使用体验。
• 用户普遍对YouTube的UI/UX设计团队的能力和决策表示质疑，认为其缺乏常识和用户考虑。

43846487.article_content:
Opened YouTube and was greeted with this abomination:
This is on a 32” 1440p display. There are five (5) videos visible, and 1/6 of
the page would have been an enormous ad.
For reference, here is YouTube as of January 2019:
There are 30 videos visible and zero ads.
I really, really hope that this A/B test fails.
Unfortunately, using an advanced analytics package I’ve projected that around
May 2026 the YouTube homepage will just be one video, and by September there
will be no videos at all on the homepage.
Presumably by then we’ll have our mandatory NeuraLinks and the YouTube algorithm
will be able to inject real-time ML generated content (and ads) straight into
our brains, tuning its output as needed to maximize our dopamine response.
I miss YouTube before they turned the pain dial all the way towards money.

data.title: Columbia student Mohsen Mahdawi is free after judge orders his release
data.author: zzzeek
data.article_summary: 哥伦比亚大学学生Mohsen Mahdawi在联邦移民羁押中获保释释放，此前他因武装国土安全部特工在佛蒙特州的入籍面试中拘留。34岁的Mahdawi是美国永久居民，出生于西岸的难民营。法官Geoffrey W. Crawford下令释放Mahdawi，政府要求暂停释放但被驳回。Mahdawi否认了政府对其支持暴力和反犹太主义行为的指控，称这些指控完全错误。他的律师称此次胜利是对Mahdawi言论自由权的捍卫，并表示将继续争取他的完全自由。Mahdawi曾组织哥伦比亚大学的亲巴勒斯坦抗议活动，政府对其的拘捕被视为对中东学生抗议活动的打压。

Columbia University student Mohsen Mahdawi is free on bail after a judge ordered his release from federal immigration custody on Wednesday, weeks after armed DHS agents detained him in Vermont during his naturalization interview.
Mahdawi, a 34-year-old U.S. permanent resident who was born and raised in a refugee camp in the West Bank, was detained April 14 and had been held at an Immigration and Customs Enforcement facility, the Northwest State Correctional Facility, in St. Albans, Vermont.
"I am saying it clear and loud to President Trump and his Cabinet: I am not afraid of you," Mahdawi said Wednesday outside the Vermont courthouse after his release.
"What we are witnessing now and what we’re understanding is exactly what Dr. Martin Luther King has said before: Injustice anywhere is a threat to justice everywhere," he added.
From the bench, Judge Geoffrey W. Crawford ordered the release of Mahdawi from prison on bail, pending the resolution of his habeas petition.

data.title: Why can't Ivies cope with losing a few hundred million?
data.author: sneakerblack
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了美国常春藤盟校在面对联邦资金削减时遇到的财务挑战。尽管这些精英大学拥有数十亿美元的捐赠基金，如哥伦比亚大学的150亿美元，但当特朗普政府扣留4亿美元联邦资金时，学校却难以应对。原因在于这些捐赠基金并不容易迅速变现，因为它们大多投资于长期项目，提前提取可能面临高额税费和投资损失。此外，学校不愿与联邦政府对抗，选择妥协而非诉讼。文章反映了精英大学在政治和财务压力下的困境。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：美国总统是否有权单方面削减或扣留大学资金，尤其是针对拥有巨额捐赠基金的顶尖大学，以及该问题所涉及的教育资源分配、大学财务管理等相关议题。

不同观点：
• **总统是否应拥有单方面扣留大学资金的权力**：
  - Kapura：认为总统不应拥有类似独裁的权力，单方面扣留大学资金是不合理的，即使文章本身回答了特定问题，但接受总统拥有这种权力是令人震惊的。
  - pjc50：质疑以学生言论为由，总统单方面扣留研究经费是否属于“言论自由”的表现。
  - linguistbreaker：明确表示总统不应拥有此权力，但同时指出常春藤盟校通过巨额捐赠基金成长，已经变得更像对冲基金而非纯粹的教育机构。

• **大学捐赠基金的管理与使用**：
  - ssalazar：指出大额捐赠基金的年度支出应限制在5%左右，以确保长期可持续性，因此扣留部分资金会对大学运营产生较大影响。
  - xnx：认为被削减的资金并非单纯的“赠与”，而是大学提供研究设施等服务的报酬，因此削减经费应被视为对服务的削减。

• **联邦资金分配的公平性与效率**：
  - steveBK123：质疑联邦资金是否应继续资助财力雄厚的常春藤盟校，而非成本效益更高的州立大学。指出常春藤盟校教育的学生数量少，但占用的联邦资源较多，认为这是对改进全国教育质量和成本的干扰。
  - strangeloops85：指出公立和私立大学之间的区别并没有想象中那么大，公立大学的州政府资助占比越来越小，并以加州大学系统为例说明联邦资金主要用于研究而非日常运营。

• **历史和政治背景的比较与警示**：
  - niemandhier：通过1930年代德国大学（如哥廷根大学和柏林大学）从世界顶尖到因政治原因衰落的例子，暗示政治干预学术机构可能带来的负面影响。

补充讨论：
• **大学财务策略的讨论**：
  - primer42：提出大学是否可以像亿万富翁用股票质押贷款一样，通过捐赠基金进行类似操作以应对资金削减的问题。
  
• **具体资金削减的影响**：
  - boplicity：强调削减的并非普通办学资金，而是研究经费，这与一般办学资金的性质不同，可能对大学的研究工作产生重大影响。

• **对政策动机的质疑**：
  - mathgradthrow：指出一些大学可能乐见政策实施，将政府作为替罪羊，以推动某些政策变化。

争议焦点：总统是否有权单方面扣留大学资金，以及这种权力是否会对学术自由和教育资源分配产生负面影响。

data.title: New Quantum GPS Backup Is 50 Times More Precise Than Alternatives
data.author: Brajeshwar
data.article_summary: 澳大利亚初创公司Q-CTRL开发了一种基于量子传感器的新型GPS备用系统，其精度比当前最先进的惯性导航系统高50倍。该系统利用 trapped ions 量子磁力计检测地球磁场的微小变化，并通过与预存磁场地图对比来精确定位，克服了传统系统因信号丢失或干扰导致的定位偏差问题。尽管该技术对电磁辐射非常敏感，但通过结合机器学习软件，能够有效消除磁噪声。该技术已在军用和航空领域引起广泛关注，并与多国国防部门和空客等公司展开合作。然而，其依赖详细的磁场地图作为参照是一大限制。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：磁图更新的频率及其全球覆盖范围，以及数据的准确性和误差边界计算

不同观点：
• solardev认为磁图的更新频率和覆盖范围需要明确，尤其是是否可以每年更新一次并保持足够的精度。他提出了对数据准确性的关注，并询问是否存在小规模波动影响精度。
• 假设的观点（未明确提出但 implied）：可能存在另一种观点认为，磁图的更新频率可以较低，因为磁场变化不大，或者小规模波动对整体精度影响有限。

补充讨论：
• solardev还询问了是否可以为任何给定的读数计算出一个误差边界，这表明他关注数据的可靠性和科学精确性。
• 讨论中隐含的争议焦点在于更新频率与精度之间的平衡，即为了保持高精度，是否需要更频繁地更新磁图，还是年度更新已经足够。

总结：
该评论主要围绕磁图的更新频率、全球覆盖范围、数据准确性以及误差边界计算展开讨论。核心在于是否年度更新能够满足精度需求，以及小规模波动和误差边界对数据可靠性的影响。

43847253.article_content:
Tech
New Quantum GPS Backup Is 50 Times More Precise Than State-of-the Art Alternatives
The quantum sensor’s extreme sensitivity makes it possible to pinpoint location with high accuracy.
Edd Gent
Apr 24, 2025
Image Credit
Tamas Tuzes-Katai on Unsplash
Share
Quantum sensors promise precision far beyond anything possible using classical technology. Australian startup Q-CTRL has put the devices to work in a GPS backup that’s 50 times better than the current state-of-the-art.
While
quantum computing
tends to garner the most headlines, there are a host of promising applications for technology that can harness the unusual effects of quantum mechanics in areas like sensing and
communication
. And a big weakness for quantum computers is actually a major benefit for quantum sensors. These systems’ sensitivity to the environment is a major source of error in quantum processors, but it also means quantum sensors can detect the most minute of changes in magnetic, electrical, and even gravitational fields.
Q-CTRL exploited these capabilities to create a device that tracks tiny changes in Earth’s magnetic field to determine its position. They designed the technology to act as a backup for GPS, which can lose signal or be deliberately jammed. In field tests, the company showed it had a tracking error 50 times lower than an inertial navigation system, the industry-standard GPS backup technology.
“We’re thrilled to be the global pioneer in taking quantum sensing from research to the field, being the first to enable real capabilities that have previously been little more than a dream,” Q-CTRL CEO and founder Michael J. Biercuk said in a
press release
.
GPS jamming is a
growing problem
, and although most commercial aircraft have an inertial navigation system as a backup, their reliability leaves plenty to be desired. These devices use motion sensors to track a vehicle from a known starting point, but errors quickly creep in and can lead to significant positioning drift within just minutes.
Q-CTRL’s system takes an entirely different approach. A quantum magnetometer made from trapped ions detects tiny variations in the Earth’s magnetic field due to changes in the structure of the surface below the aircraft. The device then compares these fluctuations to a map of the Earth’s magnetic field to determine the vehicle’s location.
The quantum sensor’s extreme sensitivity makes it possible to pinpoint location with high accuracy, but it also means it’s highly susceptible to interference from electromagnetic radiation. To get around this, Q-CTRL combined their hardware with specialized machine learning software that recognizes and removes magnetic noise from the signal.
Be Part of the Future

100% Free.
No Spam.
Unsubscribe any time.
To test the system, the company attached it to a small aircraft and carried out a series of 300-mile flights. The device pinpointed the plane’s position to within a few hundred yards throughout the flight, in contrast to an inertial navigation system that very quickly strayed several miles off the true position and got steadily worse thereafter.
The system also outperformed a range of other GPS backups, including Doppler radar and Doppler velocity lidar by a factor of 10. And unlike those approaches, the quantum navigation tech doesn’t emit any detectable signal, which could make it useful in military applications.
One limitation is that Q-CTRL’s device must compare its readings to detailed magnetic field maps, which may not always be available, Mia Jukić at the Netherlands Organization for Applied Scientific Research
told
New Scientist
. The approach always requires prominent magnetic features to act as landmarks, she added, or the navigation accuracy will suffer.
Nonetheless, the technology has caught the eye of major players in defense and aerospace. Q-CTRL is working on quantum navigation systems with the Australian Department of Defense, the US Department of Defense, the UK Royal Navy, as well as Airbus.

data.title: Wikipedia says it will use AI, but not to replace human volunteers
data.author: thm
data.article_summary: 维基百科不会用AI取代人类志愿者，因为志愿者社区是其成功的核心。维基媒体基金会的新AI战略旨在利用AI帮助志愿者克服技术障碍，提升工作效率。具体措施包括：通过AI辅助工作流支持内容审核，提升信息可发现性以节省编辑时间，自动化翻译以分享本地视角，以及通过指导加快新志愿者的加入。该战略强调以人为本，优先考虑开放源代码和透明度，并尊重隐私和人权。维基百科的使命是提供自由获取的知识，AI将帮助实现这一目标，同时维护人类的核心作用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：维基百科引入AI技术以支持志愿者和编辑工作的策略

不同观点：
• 支持引入AI以辅助志愿者和编辑工作：
  - 一些人认为AI可以帮助简化新志愿者的入门培训，比如通过UI提示或指导性辅导，从而减少贡献内容的困难度（niam, tim333）。
  - 支持者认为，AI可以在不影响内容质量的前提下，帮助自动化一些繁琐的任务，如清理和信息检索，从而让编辑有更多时间专注于人类审议和共识建立（Havoc, hexator, some_furry, the_af）。
  
• 对AI引入的潜在风险表示担忧：
  - 有人担心AI自动化翻译会导致非英语版本维基百科的质量下降（kelvinjps10, scudsworth）。
  - 一些人质疑AI是否能真正理解和执行复杂的编辑任务，尤其是涉及人类判断和本地视角的内容（scudsworth）。
  - 有人担心维基百科最终可能会变成一个AI生成内容的仓库，导致内容质量下降并形成恶性循环（the_af）。

• 对AI技术实际应用效果的怀疑：
  - 有人认为AI在维基百科的应用可能只是表面功夫，用来满足机器学习官员的考核（scudsworth）。
  - 有人质疑AI技术的引入是否真的能提高效率，还是最终会浪费志愿者的时间和精力，尤其是在让志愿者学习AI课程方面（niam）。

• 对维基百科商业化倾向的批评：
  - 有人担心维基百科会转向开发AI研究产品，并将其出售给大学或消费者，从而偏离其非盈利性质（film42, notorandit, NotAnOtter, rvz）。
  - 不过，也有支持者指出，维基媒体作为一个非盈利组织，其对AI的引入显得更为理智和务实，并且强调人类志愿者的重要性（some_furry, ChrisArchitect）。

补充讨论：
• 关于AI在维基百科中的具体应用形式的争议，比如是否应该使用AI进行自动化翻译和内容生成，以及如何避免AI生成内容的质量问题。
• 对维基百科现有编辑环境的批评，指出新贡献者在贡献内容时往往缺乏指导和反馈，这也是引入AI辅导的动机之一。
• 对维基百科引入AI的长期影响的猜测和担忧，尤其是涉及商业化倾向和内容质量控制方面。

43846052.article_content:
Not too long ago, we were asked when we're going to replace Wikipedia's human-curated knowledge with AI.
The answer? We're not.
The community of volunteers behind Wikipedia is the most important and unique element of Wikipedia’s success. For nearly 25 years, Wikipedia editors have researched, deliberated, discussed, built consensus, and collaboratively written the largest encyclopedia humankind has ever seen. Their care and commitment to reliable encyclopedic knowledge is something AI cannot replace.
That is why our new AI strategy doubles down on the volunteers behind Wikipedia.
We will use AI to build features that remove technical barriers to allow the humans at the core of Wikipedia to spend their valuable time on what they want to accomplish, and not on how to technically achieve it. Our investments will be focused on specific areas where generative AI excels, all in the service of creating unique opportunities that will boost Wikipedia’s volunteers:
Supporting Wikipedia’s moderators and patrollers
with AI-assisted workflows that automate tedious tasks in support of knowledge integrity;
Giving Wikipedia’s editors time back
by improving the discoverability of information on Wikipedia to leave more time for human deliberation, judgment, and consensus building;
Helping editors share local perspectives or context
by automating the translation and adaptation of common topics;
Scaling the onboarding of new Wikipedia volunteers
with guided mentorship.
We believe that our future work with AI will be successful not only because of
what
we do, but
how
we do it. Our efforts will use our long-held values,
principles
, and policies (like
privacy
and
human rights
) as a compass: we will take a human-centered approach and will prioritize human agency; we will prioritize using open-source or open-weight AI; we will prioritize transparency; and we will take a nuanced approach to multilinguality, a fundamental part of Wikipedia.
Providing freely accessible knowledge to anyone on the planet is Wikipedia’s mission, one that has only grown in importance since the rise of generative AI. Its success is why Wikipedia is at the core of every AI training model. With this new AI strategy, we are making a promise and a commitment to the world we serve and the volunteers who have made—continue to make—Wikipedia the largest encyclopedia that humanity has ever known.
You can read the Wikimedia Foundation’s new AI strategy over on
Meta-Wiki
.
—
Chris Albon is the
Director of Machine Learning
at the Wikimedia Foundation. You can follow him at @
chrisalbon
. Leila Zia is the
Head of Research
at the Wikimedia Foundation.

data.title: Firefox tab groups are here
data.author: TangerineDream
data.article_summary: Firefox推出了标签页分组功能，这是根据Mozilla Connect社区平台上超过4500名用户的反馈开发的。该功能允许用户将标签页拖放到分组中，并按名称或颜色进行标记，以保持浏览器的整洁和专注。开发团队通过深入分析用户的评论和需求，设计了这个兼具灵活性和简洁性的功能。目前，团队还在试验智能标签组，利用AI根据打开的标签页自动建议分组名称，同时确保用户隐私不外泄。这一功能的推出得益于社区的积极参与和反馈，未来Firefox将继续倾听用户意见，进一步优化产品。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Mozilla推出的标签组功能及其相关问题

不同观点：
• **支持与赞赏**：
   - hardwaresofton认为该功能是用户强烈要求的，赞赏Mozilla实现此功能，并计划从第三方扩展切换到内置功能。
   - m4r1k表示该功能加上新的简化版配置管理器，使他可以完全放弃Chrome。
   - AdmiralAsshat通过实际使用体验，认为标签组功能显著提升了他的工作效率，尤其是在多任务处理时。

• **批评与不满**：
   - eviks指出当前界面的多个问题，如强制命名、无法单键解散组、拖放操作不精确等，并提到一些用户请求多年未被实现。
   - dizhn批评公告中缺少关键信息，如功能是否已在稳定版中推出、如何启用等，并质疑Mozilla是否会处理长期存在的bug。
   - surajrmal对功能推出时间过长表示不满，并认为设计上与Chrome类似，可能只是为了与AI功能竞争。
   - bityard提到Firefox曾经有过类似功能（Panorama），但因使用率低被移除，质疑这次能否持久。

• **功能使用与用户体验**：
   - canadianwriter对其他用户大量打开标签的习惯感到好奇，并讨论是否与书签和历史记录功能不足有关。
   - Kim_Bruning习惯使用Tree Style Tabs插件，无法理解没有该插件如何工作。
   - neogodless希望该功能能与多账户容器集成，以便更方便地管理标签。
   - guerby对UI设计不满，尤其是拖放创建标签组的操作，认为容易误操作且无法移动整个组。

• **同步问题**：
   - aucisson_masque提到标签组信息不会同步到移动设备，可能需要再等三年。
   - penguin_booze指出标签组无法在不同设备间同步，导致在另一台设备上显示为随机标签。

补充讨论：
- 用户对标签组功能的需求和使用习惯各异，有人认为非常有用，有人则对功能设计和实现不满。
- 功能同步问题是一个争议点，尤其是在多设备使用场景下。
- 一些用户对Mozilla的历史问题和功能移除仍有疑虑，担心新功能是否能持久。

43834101.article_content:
Firefox
You asked, we built it: Firefox tab groups are here
April 29, 2025
Jenifer Boscacci
What happens when 4,500 people ask for the same feature? At Firefox, we build it.
Firefox tab groups now available
Tab groups
have long been the most
requested idea
on
Mozilla Connect
– our community platform – and thanks to thousands of votes, comments and passionate feedback, it’s finally here. 🎉
But this is more than just a feature launch. It’s the story of what happens when community insight, real-world pain points, and a whole lot of curiosity come together.
A feature the community asked for, loud and clear
Just one day after Mozilla Connect quietly
launched
in March 2022, a
request
for tab groups appeared. We hadn’t even promoted the platform. There were no announcements. But the community found Mozilla Connect and rallied behind the request for tab groups.
“It’s still the number one most upvoted post on Mozilla Connect,” said Jon Siddoway, who helps surface user insights to Firefox teams. “Even when the feature was in beta, people were still voting for it and saying, ‘We want this.’”
At Mozilla, we work hard to make Firefox the best browser for you. Last year, we
shared
what we were working on – features that help you stay organized, like our handy sidebar,
vertical tabs
and tab groups. As we noted then, community feedback directly shaped what came next.
“It’s still the number one most upvoted post on Mozilla Connect.”
Jon Siddoway, product manager of Mozilla Connect
That early request kicked off a collaboration between the Firefox team and community. Before any code was written, Jon summarized comments, tracked trends across 64+ pages of feedback and brought key themes to the team.
That enthusiasm spilled into beta testing. Before the official
invite
to community members went out, many of them discovered the hidden toggle in the Nightly release, turned it on themselves, and started sharing how to use it. The team watched, learned and iterated from the sidelines.
Listening and learning from thousands of voices
Stefan Smagula, product manager for the tabs group feature, didn’t just skim the posts – he dove in.
“I read Mozilla Connect every day for the first month,” he said. “Sometimes the ideas confirmed what we were already thinking. Other times they were totally new and unexpected, like requests for nested tab groups.”
But with over 1,000 comments and many differing opinions, how do you make decisions?
“Sometimes the ideas confirmed what we were already thinking. Other times they were totally new and unexpected.”
Stefan Smagula, product manager at Firefox
“You try to get to the
underlying needs
behind each request,” Stefan explained. “Instead of just implementing one person’s idea, you look for the broader pattern — the thing that could help the most people.”
This approach helped shape a feature that balances flexibility with simplicity. With tab groups, you can drag and drop tabs into organized groups, label them by name or color, and stay focused. Whether you’re a
minimalist
with 10 tabs or a power user juggling 10,000 (seriously — one of our colleagues does this), tab groups can help.
Keep it together — group your tabs by trip, work, or whatever you need!
“Tab groups aren’t just about decluttering,” Stefan said. “It’s about reclaiming your flow and finding focus again.”
It also reinforced the team’s belief that done is never truly done.
“Tab groups aren’t just about decluttering. It’s about reclaiming your flow and finding focus again.”
Stefan Smagula, product manager at Firefox
What’s next: Make tab groups smarter
Once early testers began using tab groups in
Firefox Nightly and Beta
, feedback kept rolling in – both on Mozilla Connect and in places like
Reddit
and X, where Stefan scouts for feedback. Many users wanted less friction and more flow when managing their tabs, which inspired the team to explore the next step: having the browser help organize things automatically.
Now, the team is experimenting with smart tab groups, a new AI-powered feature that suggests names and groups based on the tabs you have open. Other browsers might send your tab info to the cloud, but Firefox keeps it on your device. Your tabs stay private and never leave your device.
“I used to have 30 windows open, each with 30 or 40 tabs. Smart tab groups changed the way I work. It made it easier to find what I need and resume tasks faster,” said Stefan.
It’s just the beginning of what’s possible when you pair smart tech with real human needs.
“I used to have 30 windows open, each with 30 or 40 tabs. Smart tab groups changed the way I work. It made it easier to find what I need and resume tasks faster.”
Stefan Smagula, product manager at Firefox
Thank you – and keep the ideas coming
This feature wouldn’t exist without you. Your upvotes, comments, ideas and testing helped bring it to life.
As Stefan put it: “It’s extremely motivating to know how many people want this. It makes the hard work easier and more meaningful.”

data.title: Why the lettering on Pope Francis's tomb looks so bad
data.author: Tomte
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：评论者对文章未解释“为什么”以及问题严重性的看法存在不同观点。

不同观点：
• [duxup] 认为文章没有解释问题的根本原因，并将该问题视为小题大做，形容其为“把小问题搞成大问题”。该评论者似乎对文章的深度和解释力表示不满，认为问题并没有文章所暗示的那么严重。

• [oatsandsugar] 则以调侃的方式回应，期待有人能像丹·布朗的小说一样挖掘出该问题的深层意义。这暗示评论者可能认为问题本身具有一定的戏剧性或神秘性，值得被进一步探讨和解读，甚至有些夸张地期待更复杂或隐秘的背景。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于问题的严重性和是否有必要对其进行深入解释。一方认为问题被过度放大，另一方则以戏谑的方式期待更深的解读。

• 两个评论都对文章的不满有所体现，但表达方式不同：一个是直接批评缺乏解释，另一个则是通过幽默表达对问题戏剧化的期待。

dht.lookup(infoHash, [callback])
Find peers for the given info hash.
This does a recursive lookup in the DHT. Potential peers that are discovered are emitted
as

peer
event below for more info.

,

properties.

port
the implied port option will be set and other peers will use the public
dht port as your announced port.
If
dht.announce
is called soon (< 5 minutes) after
dht.lookup
, then the routing table
generated during the lookup can be re-used, because the "tokens" sent by each node will

dht.lookup
will
first be performed to discover relevant nodes and get valid "tokens" from each of them.

A "token" is an opaque value that must be presented for a node to announce that its
controlling peer is downloading a torrent. It must present the token received from the
same queried node in a recent query for peers. This is to prevent malicious hosts from
signing up other hosts for torrents.
All token management is handled internally by this
module.
callback
will be called when the announce operation has completed, and is called with
a single parameter that is an
Error
or null.

data.article_summary: 美国众议院交通与基础设施委员会将讨论预算法案，其中包含对电动车和混合动力车的新年度注册费用。电动车将被征收200美元，混合动力车100美元，而柴油车如福特F-350 Duramax的车主仅需支付20美元，且2030年前免费。该费用将随通胀逐年增加，直至2034年或2035年到期。尽管该法案不能强制各州收取费用，但若不遵守，联邦将扣留部分 highway 基金。委员会主席Sam Graves称此举旨在公平，让电动车为公路使用付费，但批评者认为此举打击清洁能源政策，可能阻碍电动车普及，且无法根本解决公路信托基金的资金问题。环保组织谴责此法案是对清洁交通的惩罚，而非激励。

主要讨论点：关于对电动车主征税以资助道路建设的讨论

不同观点：
• **billy99k的观点**：提到民主党计划对安装太阳能板的用户征税，并提议对电动车主征税以资助道路建设。这是因为电动车主支付的燃油税较少，而燃油税通常用于道路维护。这一观点暗示了对电动车主征税的合理性，以确保他们在道路维护上也尽一份责任。

• **bhandziuk的观点**：以自身为例，指出在乔治亚州，电动车主每年需要支付220美元的注册费，这已经比内燃机汽车（ICE）车主支付的费用高。bhandziuk质疑如果新的征税提案通过，是否意味着每年需要支付高达420美元的费用，暗示这种额外征税可能不公平，尤其是电动车主已经支付了较高的费用。

• **philipallstar的观点**：提到所谓的"特斯拉国家控制"（state capture by Tesla），暗示这可能是特斯拉或其他电动车企业对政府决策的影响，可能是在批评政府为电动车主增加税收是受到特定企业利益驱动的结果，而非基于公平或实际需求。

WASHINGTON, DC—The House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee will meet today to discuss its proposed budget legislation, and there's a doozy in there for drivers of electric vehicles and hybrids. As part of the Republican Party's ongoing war against
science
and
the environment
under President Trump, committee chairperson Sam Graves (R-Mo.) has included some new annual fees that will cost all drivers some, but some drivers more.
Republicans plan to use the
budget reconciliation process
to pass this legislation, which is an expedited process that removes some of the US Senate's ability to stall. They're proposing a new annual federal motor vehicle registration fee, which state DMVs would have to collect and pass back to the federal government.
If it passes, all battery EVs would be subject to a new $200 tax. Hybrids—defined as vehicles that are propelled by both an electric motor and an internal combustion engine or other power source (which would include fuel cell EVs)—will pay $100. But someone who commutes 90 miles a day in a particulate-belching Ford F-350 Duramax diesel pickup truck gets away with a mere $20 a year, and only from October 1, 2030; until then they get to drive for free.
To make things even better, the bill requires these fees to be linked to inflation and should be increased each year, until 2034 when the tax expires for unelectrified vehicles, or 2035, the last year that EVs and hybrids would be taxed like this. So, a $200 registration fee in 2026 becomes a $250 registration fee in 2035.
Not everyone will have to pay, however. The bill exempts commercial vehicles, which should see a rush from tax avoiders to register their vehicles under their businesses, similar to what we saw during the George W. Bush administration, when a change in the tax law meant businesses
could claim a $100,000 tax credit
if they purchased a truck or SUV that weighed more than 6,000 lbs. Farm vehicles are also exempt from the law.
With EV adoption as low as it is in the US, the sums raised by these EV and hybrid charges will be essentially a rounding error in the federal budget, which this year should top $7 trillion. The Eno Center for Transportation calculates that this new tax will contribute an extra $110 billion to the highway Trust Fund by 2035 but that cuts to other taxes and more spending mean that the fund will still be $222 billion short of its commitments—assuming that this added fee doesn't further dampen EV adoption in the US, that is.
The committee cannot mandate that states collect these new taxes on drivers. But just as the federal government used the withholding of federal highway funds as a stick to force all states to raise the drinking age to 21, this bill would require the Department of Transportation to withhold 125 percent of the estimated total registration fees if it did not comply.
Graves' justification for this regressive attack on clean energy policies is that it's merely a matter of fairness, with a healthy side helping of the usual grievance politics. "Our proposal more than offsets these historic investments and reduces the deficit with rescissions of wasteful Green New Deal style spending from the Inflation Reduction Act and ensuring that electric vehicles begin paying their share for their use of the nation’s highways. It’s only fair that EVs pay these user fees like other motorists. In fact, the new user fees provision addresses the broken Highway Trust Fund revenue stream in a substantial manner for the first time in over 30 years," Graves said in a statement.
Making this move even more regressive, Graves notes in his statement that the vast majority of US states—39 in total—already charge
EV drivers a registration fee
, and 28 do the same for hybrid drivers. Graves also hints at the end of a federal gasoline tax, despite
ever-increasing levels of atmospheric CO
2
and the unequivocal evidence that this is caused by fossil fuel emissions.
"House Republicans are threatening to take away billions of dollars in funding that will help to slash health-threatening pollution, improve walkability, and rebuild communities harmed by highways," said Katherine Garcia, director of Sierra Club Clean Transportation for All.
"They're also trying to punish EV and hybrid drivers with an excessive annual fee rather than fixing the unsustainable Highway Trust Fund. Now is the time to incentivize, not penalize, people to drive cleaner vehicles that curb pollution harmful to our health and climate. Rather than spreading misinformation and attacking popular programs, Congress must focus on ensuring more Americans have access to clean transportation options. This proposal to shift critical funding and impose a punitive fee on Americans to pay for billionaire tax cuts is unacceptable."
Jonathan M. Gitlin
Automotive Editor
Jonathan M. Gitlin

data.title: Show HN: A Chrome extension that will auto-reject non-essential cookies
data.author: mitch292
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了名为"Reject Cookies"的Chrome扩展程序，旨在自动拒绝网站的非必要Cookie，从而避免频繁出现的Cookie同意横幅。文章提到当前有一些自动接受Cookie的扩展，但缺乏自动拒绝的解决方案。该扩展首先尝试拒绝Cookie，若不成功则关闭横幅，符合GDPR等法规要求。扩展使用了一组常见选择器和特定供应商的逻辑来实现这一功能，代码开源。实施过程中，作者利用了Cursor和Vibe编码，并提供了权限配置和示例代码。扩展仍在完善中，欢迎用户反馈和报告问题以覆盖更多用例。
data.comments_summary:

不同观点：

Add the extension
A Chrome Extension
Everyone can agree that cookie consent banners are frustrating. It might be one of the few unifying factors on the internet today. Even though it’s a couple clicks, the couple clicks are a pain, and the couple clicks can happen on many sites each day.
There are browser extensions out there that will auto-accept cookies like
I don’t care about cookies
and it’s open source fork
I still don’t care about cookies
. You can even chain this extension with another that will auto-clean up your cookies. This is an adequate solution and ascribes to
unix philosophy
.
Additionally, there are extensions like
uBlock Origin
with additional filters to help ignore these annoying pop ups. Or
Privacy Badger
to block cookie trackers. Although there is space to provide an extension that just auto-rejects non essential cookies.
That’s what led to the “Reject Cookies” chrome extension. It will first attempt to reject the cookies on the page. If that is unsuccessful, it will then attempt to close the cookie pop up or banner. To comply with the regulations governing cookies under the
GDPR and the ePrivacy Directive you must
Receive users’ consent before you use any cookies except strictly necessary cookies.
So the omission of an acceptance should be on par with an explicit rejection. If you’re interested in how it works the code is
open source and on github
, but let’s step through it at a high level.
How it’s implemented
Vibe coding is the answer. I leveraged Cursor and let it auto-select the model. This combination while extremely useful, did not serve me as well as recent past experience. On the project setup front, I had not previously written a Chrome extension. Having the Cursor agent set up the boilerplate was convenient. Although, it requested too liberal of permissions in the permissions to start and wouldn’t go and update them as the design of the app changed. Below is a snippet of the
manifest.json
to show what the permissions ended up looking like.

The problem was once again these selectors were extremely liberal things like elements with the class “accept”. I opted to take a more targeted approach and aim the logic at specific cookie consent vendors that most sites seem to leverage. Cursor’s agent was, as expected, not able to help much with this implementation.

Help it get better
Reject Cookies is still a work in progress.
It can use your support to help cover more use cases and report bugs. As mentioned the design targets specific cookie consent implementations from different vendors. There are more vendors out there and different flavors of each vendors implementation. The side panel allows you to report sites where the cookie consent rejection was missed along with a place to report bugs or issues with the extension. The side panel can be accessed by clicking on the chrome extension’s menu in Chrome. You can also feel free to reach out to

data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary:
这篇文章讨论了性能优化的困难之处，主要包括以下几点：

1. **组合性**：某些优化只能一起工作，而有些组合则会导致性能下降。选择正确的优化组合需要深厚的知识和经验。
   
2. **剪枝和试错**：去除明显的次优方案往往依赖于启发式方法。优化通常需要大量的试错，无法单靠直觉，必须进行性能分析（profiling）。

3. **连续性**：一些算法需要选择参数和优化边界，例如混合排序算法和FFT，小改动可能导致性能剧变。持续的重新 benchmarking 是必要的。

4. **不兼容性**：某些优化由于外部限制而失败，例如两个查找表（LUT）无法同时放入缓存。这种情况下，需要通过分块等技巧尝试解决。

文章最后建议将优化工作分配给多人进行，开源项目尤其受益。同时，作者提倡建立自动寻找最佳参数的测试平台，以减轻手动优化的负担。

• [compiler-guy] 提到Apple的LLVM分支缺乏对Apple Silicon的调度注解，指出虽然开发者可能无法获取某些数据，但不代表这些数据不存在。

• [hinkley] 将优化比作节食，强调坚持和系统化的方法，而非依赖“神奇技巧”。
• [somethingsome] 教授学生使用树状图跟踪有希望的优化路径，结合大量使用分析工具，逐步缩小优化范围，最终找到最优解。
• [karmakaze] 认为在大多数情况下，初始选择远非最优，任何更好的选择都是改进，但对于前沿领域的优化需要更具创造性和系统性的努力。
• [MatthiasWandel] 提到数据依赖性对性能的影响，指出重用刚刚计算出的数据可能导致流水线气泡。
• [PaulKeeble] 指出微观优化中算法分析和硬件直觉之间的差距，强调工具可以帮助识别低效之处，但无法预测更改会如何改善性能。
• [mannyv] 认为优化需要深入理解系统工作原理，本质上是调试和故障排除，但目标不同。
• [enescakir] 指出最难处理的错误往往是在“优化”后才显现出来。

补充讨论：
• 优化过程中测量与理论分析的关系：[jmull] 和 [ttd] 讨论了工具观察与理论建模的互补性，而 [willvarfar] 则区分了微观和宏观优化的不同策略。
• 自动化与手动优化的权衡：[hansvm] 和 [somethingsome] 分享了自动化工具和系统方法在优化中的应用，而 [karmakaze] 则强调了人类创造力和系统性努力在优化前沿领域的重要性。
• 优化工具和编译器的局限性：[compiler-guy] 和 [Validark] 提到了当前工具和编译器的不足，并讨论了未来可能的改进方向。

43831705.article_content:
Why performance optimization is hard work
April 29, 2025
Hacker News
Reddit
I’m not talking about skill, knowledge, or convincing a world focused on radical acceleration that optimization is necessary. Performance optimization is hard because it’s fundamentally a brute-force task, and there’s nothing you can do about it.
This post is a bit of a rant on my frustrations with code optimization. I’ll also try to give actionable advice, which I hope enchants your experience.
Composability
Certain optimizations can only work together, while others lead to pessimizations when combined. To be an expert means to know what optimization avenues exist; to be a master means to know which ones to choose.
I have a post on integer formatting in the works, covering a very particular algorithm design – and I
still
haven’t finished it because there’s like five different choices to make, I have no idea how they impact each other, and I need to analyze
2
5
variants to claim which one’s the best in conscience. Several of my projects are similarly stuck because I don’t have the willpower to implement a dozen combinations.
Pruning “obviously” suboptimal approaches is all but a heuristic. I like to think I’m more in tune with an x86-64 CPU than most people, and it still manages to surprise me from time to time. Dumb algorithms can become more applicable due to vectorization, smart code can fail due to
branch misprediction
or
store-to-load forwarding
gone wrong.
Optimization takes a lot of trial and error. I dislike the “intuition doesn’t work, profile your code” mantra because it seemingly says profiling is a viable replacement for theoretical calculations, which it isn’t. But I can’t argue that profiling is avoidable. I often joke that
perf report
is my go-to disassembler.
Worse yet, you can’t trust “obviously” good code either. In
a previous post
, I optimized a single linear pass by replacing it with a superlinear sort. This is by no means a unique experience: just yesterday, I saw someone optimize best-of-class
Barrett reduction
by dividing the numbers as
double
s, rounding them, and computing the reminder from the quotient. It’s so stupid that it can’t possibly work, yet it does.
The good news is that the work here can be split among multiple people trying different approaches. Open-source projects in particular benefit from this, because contributors typically have different strengths and focus on different ideas. Try to reuse work by consulting your teammates or reading about others’ experiences in solving similar tasks.
Continuity
A variation on this is algorithms where a
cut-off boundary
is present. You no longer choose whether to apply an optimization: you also need to select parameters via more trial and error. For example:
Hybrid sorting algorithms can switch between different implementations due to high big-O constants,
FFT
can switch between recursive and iterative approaches to better utilize processor cache.
Depending on data density, the optimal set structure might be bitsets, hash sets, or complementary hash sets.
Modifying either of the alternative algorithms requires rebenchmarking to update the optimal boundary. Small modifications here can lead to
drastic
end performance changes due to interactions with CPU cache, branch and memory access prediction, the discrete nature of recursive cut-offs, and floating-point precision (for
big integer multiplication via FFT
). Forgetting to rebenchmark and abandoning a prospective approach can easily leave
2
×
performance on the table.
For another example, consider a program that executes
n
times either action
A
or
B
depending on probability
p
. If
p
is far from
1
2
, branch prediction means it’s better to implement the switch with an
if
; if
p
is close to
1
2
, branch prediction will fail and a branchless approach will work better. Not only does the relative performance of
A
and
B
matter here, but the cost of branch misprediction matters as well, and that might depend not only on the CPU but on the precise code executed.
Ideally, you’d have a test bench that plots graphs and finds optimal parameter values automatically, even though getting this working can be draining. This way, running checks all the time becomes cheap and emotionally easier. Even if it takes half an hour, you can still work on something else in parallel.
Incompatibility
The worst example of incompatible optimizations is those that fail due to external constraints.
One example is when two
LUTs
don’t fit in cache together, but do individually. You can sometimes fix this by splitting the computation into multiple passes, where each pass only needs to access helper data that does fit into cache. This does not necessarily mean two passes over
all
data, consuming
2
×
memory bandwidth – you can chunk the data and apply two passes on a chunk, which increases performance if the chunk fits into, say, L3. But sometimes that doesn’t work, and then I bash my head against the wall.

• [enescakir] 指出最难处理的错误往往是在“优化”后才显现出来。

补充讨论：
• 优化过程中测量与理论分析的关系：[jmull] 和 [ttd] 讨论了工具观察与理论建模的互补性，而 [willvarfar] 则区分了微观和宏观优化的不同策略。
• 自动化与手动优化的权衡：[hansvm] 和 [somethingsome] 分享了自动化工具和系统方法在优化中的应用，而 [karmakaze] 则强调了人类创造力和系统性努力在优化前沿领域的重要性。
• 优化工具和编译器的局限性：[compiler-guy] 和 [Validark] 提到了当前工具和编译器的不足，并讨论了未来可能的改进方向。

data.title: Linux Kernel Exploitation: Attack of the Vsock
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 本文描述了一次针对Linux内核漏洞CVE-2025-21756的深入研究与利用过程。该漏洞存在于vsock（虚拟套接字）中，当传输重新分配时，可能会错误地减少引用计数，导致"释放后使用"（UAF）漏洞。作者通过分析补丁，设置QEMU和GDB调试环境，成功复现并利用该漏洞。最初，作者尝试进行跨缓存攻击，通过释放并重新分配vsock对象，以图操控消息对象中的函数指针来实现代码执行。在调试过程中，作者成功触发了内核恐慌（kernel panic），确认了UAF漏洞的存在。然而，由于AppArmor和LSM（Linux安全模块）的阻碍，进一步的利用受到限制。最终，作者通过不断调试和修改，成功绕过部分障碍，实现权限提升。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Linux内核漏洞利用与安全性

不同观点：
• [klysm] 认为为了项目牺牲GPA是有趣的经历，暗示在技术探索中，学术成绩可能不是首要的，实践和项目经验更加重要。
• [chc4] 对具体技术细节进行了讨论，认为将UaF（Use-after-Free）转化为类型混淆攻击是更有效的手段，并详细描述了可能的技术路径，例如通过喷射更多的sockets来实现类型混淆攻击，从而获取内存读写权限。
• [snvzz] 提出Linux内核由于代码量巨大，必然存在bug，因此建议考虑采用更安全的系统设计，例如seL4，这是一种更加安全的操作系统设计。
• [xyst] 提到了Rust for Linux项目的必要性，认为当前Linux内核维护者对Rust的抵制态度导致了原本参与该项目的开发者离开，暗示Rust可能是一种提高内核安全性的解决方案。

补充讨论：
• [mperham] 提到编码问题，虽然没有深入讨论，但指出了可能存在的技术问题。
• [grg0] 对文章质量表示赞赏，并引用了另一个RSA教程作为例子，显示出对技术内容的认可。
• [Dwedit] 简单提到了"Rop Chains"（面向返回编程链），这是一种常用于漏洞利用的技术，但未展开详细讨论。
• [dang] 认为讨论偏离主题，因此标注为"offtopic"。

争议焦点：
• 关于Linux内核的安全性问题，[snvzz] 认为应当转向seL4这样的安全设计，而[xyst] 则认为Rust for Linux是更好的解决方案，显示出在如何提升内核安全性上的不同立场。
• [chc4] 提出的技术路径与其他评论的技术讨论形成对比，显示出在漏洞利用技术细节上的不同看法。

总结：讨论围绕Linux内核的漏洞利用、编码问题以及安全性提升方案展开，涉及到具体技术细节、替代操作系统设计以及Rust语言的应用前景等多个方面。争议主要集中在如何有效提升Linux内核的安全性。

data.title: JetBrains defends removal of negative reviews for unpopular AI Assistant
data.author: przemub
data.article_summary: JetBrains为其删除AI Assistant插件市场上的负面评价辩护，称此举是根据其政策或为了移除过时内容。其AI Assistant自2023年7月发布以来下载量超过2200万次，但评分仅为2.3（满分5分）。用户发现一些负面评价被删除，引发不满，认为这是为了提升评分。JetBrains解释称，这些评价提到的问题已解决或因包含不当语言等违反政策。尽管推出新AI代理Junie并增加免费 tier，但由于AI服务成本高昂，用户仍抱怨Junie过于昂贵。JetBrains的商业模式依赖付费订阅，而其产品如IntelliJ IDEA广受好评，但新UI设计仍有争议。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：JetBrains删除产品评论的行为及其AI插件的质量和方向

不同观点：
• **反对删除评论**：[ziddoap]和[JumpCrisscross]认为，JetBrains删除提到已解决问题的老评论是不合理的。他们认为，即使问题已经解决，这些评论对潜在买家仍有价值，删除评论会降低对公司透明度的信任。评论被删除本身传递了一个负面信号。[terminalbraid]补充，这种行为表明JetBrains没有从过去的错误中吸取教训。

• **支持通过其他方式处理评论**：[cadamsdotcom]和[reactordev]建议，JetBrains可以通过回复评论并通知用户更新状态，而不是直接删除评论。这种方式既能解决问题，也能显示公司对用户的关心。[reactordev]进一步提出，应激励用户在问题解决后重新评价产品。

• **对JetBrains的AI方向感到失望**：[buremba]和[terminalbraid]认为，JetBrains在AI功能上的投入偏离了其核心优势，尤其是在AI并非所有用户都需要的情况下。他们担心这种趋势会影响IDE的整体质量和用户体验，甚至可能导致“IDE冬季”的到来。[buybackoff]同样表达了对现有用户资源被用于开发AI功能的担忧，认为这偏离了用户的实际需求。

• **对JetBrains产品的整体评价**：[zer0-c00l]和[steve-atx-7600]表示，尽管他们喜欢JetBrains的产品，但在AI功能上，JetBrains的表现不如Cursor和Windsurf等其他插件。而[endofreach]则认为，JetBrains相较于其他公司更特殊，允许犯更多错误，但应避免被AI潮流所裹挟。

• **对JetBrains服务和条款的不满**：[unfunco]提到，在取消订阅时，JetBrains没有提供任何反馈选项，且对条款更改没有详细解释，显示出对用户意见的不重视。[mrlonglong]则以个人立场表示，作为付费用户，他更希望自己思考问题，而不是依赖AI助手。

补充讨论：
• **具体插件评价**：[JumpCrisscross]详细评价了JetBrains的AI插件，指出其在第三方支持、性能和功能上的不足。虽然新版本有所改进，但整体仍不尽如人意。[chuckadams]则提到了其他AI插件如Junie和Augment，认为它们在某些方面优于JetBrains的AI Assistant。

争议焦点：
• **删除评论的合理性**：用户认为删除评论是不透明的做法，降低了用户对JetBrains的信任，而JetBrains可能认为这是为了保持评论的时效性和准确性。

43850377.article_content:
AI/ML
Development
JetBrains has defended its removal of negative reviews and feedback for its AI Assistant on its plugin marketplace, stating that this was either in accordance with its policy or to remove outdated content.
The AI Assistant, first released in July 2023, has been downloaded over 22 million times but is rated only 2.3 out of 5. Users this week noticed that some negative reviews were being removed. “My previous comment was deleted without any specific reason. Jetbrains seems to be deleting negative reviews, which destroyed my confidence and trust in this company. They do not value their customers and their feedback anymore. I still give it 1 star, because it installed automatically and is slow and buggy,”
said one
today.
Reaction on social media was to see this as a desperate attempt to improve ratings; but a JetBrains employee
said
that reviews were removed because they mentioned issues that had since been solved, or because they violated
policy
such as “swearing, etc.”
The spokesperson added that the company could have done better and said that “Nuking several reviews at once without a heads-up looked shady. At least, we should’ve posted a notice and provided more details to the authors.”
The incident has drawn attention though to the AI Assistant’s poor reputation. One developer
restated
their deleted post perhaps in more moderate terms, but said that issues include limited support for third-party model providers, which “is restricted to chat operations only,” noticeable latency, frequent delays, core features locked to JetBrains cloud services, inconsistent user experience across project types, and sparse documentation.
Another common complaint is that the AI Assistant installs itself without permission. A user on Reddit called it “the annoying self-healing/reinstalling phoenix of a plug-in.”
JetBrains referred us to the Reddit post linked above when we asked for comment on the deleted reviews.
AI services are expensive to provide, because they tend to be processor-intensive, but competition between vendors is a likely reason for JetBrains introducing a
free tier
earlier this month, as well as a new AI agent called Junie, intended to run alongside AI Assistant. Junie has been better received that the older AI plugin, though cost is an issue. “Junie is a great tool, but it’s far too expensive. With the current AI Pro plan, my token quota was used up in just three days,”
said
one user.
Unlike competitors such as Microsoft, AWS or Google, JetBrains markets only developer tools and services, and does not have a separate cloud business to fall back on. Products such as the free Visual Studio Code (VS Code) have put pressure on JetBrains to be more generous with community editions of its products, but its business model depends on paying subscribers.
JetBrains IDEs including IntelliJ IDEA for Java and Rider for C# are well liked, though its gradual introduction of a new UI
continues to be contentious
.

data.title: Google Play sees 47% decline in apps since start of last year
data.author: GeekyBear
data.article_summary: 2024年至今，Google Play上的应用数量从约340万锐减至180万，下降了47%，而同期苹果App Store的应用数量略有增加。这一变化主要是由于Google提高了应用质量要求，清除了低质量、功能单一或无实际功能的应用，以改善用户体验并帮助开发者提高可见度。Google还加强了审核机制，防止欺诈应用，并禁止未提供必要信息的开发者账户。尽管欧盟的新贸易法规也可能影响部分应用下架，但苹果同样实施了该政策却未见应用数量减少。Appfigures数据显示，Google Play的应用发布量在2024年有所增加，但整体数量仍在下降。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Google Play 控制台对开发者的新要求及其影响

不同观点：
• Lammy：认为 Google 的新要求（如 DUNS 号码）对个体开发者不友好，即使是免费和离线软件也受到影响，且 Google 的沟通方式显得他们只针对公司而非个人开发者。
• serial_dev：指出独立开发者或业余项目在 Play 商店发布应用不合理，需要经过繁琐的程序且面临被下架的风险，建议转向其他技术平台。
• fidotron：认为欧盟的新规则（要求开发者共享姓名和地址）可能是导致这些变化的原因。
• jsnell：批评应用测试要求不合理，特别是对非企业开发者，认为这会阻碍新开发者进入。
• leesalminen：描述了非西方国家开发者在获取 DUNS 号码时面临的高成本和复杂程序。
• dusted：反对在免费应用上强制公开个人地址，认为这是对个人隐私的侵犯。
• GeekyBear：提到 Google 提高 API 级别要求对一些已建立的应用造成影响，如 iA Writer 退出。
• zmmmmm：认为 Google 不再关心激励开发者，移动 OS 大战结束后，大公司倾向于通过提高门槛来自我保护。
• kshri24：批评 FAANG 公司将官僚主义与技术结合，自动化掉了客户服务而非官僚程序。
• mullingitover：支持 Google 清理无价值应用，质疑此前为何允许这些应用存在。
• mvieira38：希望去中心化的应用分发模式取代当前的应用商店模式，反对 Google 对用户数据的掌控。
• pjmlp：认为当前应用过剩，对 "每个需求都有一个应用" 的时代已过去，开发者被迫为创新而更新应用。
• jonplackett：比较 iOS 和 Android 的开发体验，认为 Play 商店的开发体验较差。
• phendrenad2：怀念 Android 早期多样化的个人开发者应用，认为 Play 商店算法和次级应用商店的衰落导致这些应用消失。
• delduca：因官僚程序退出 Play 商店。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：Google 的新要求是否合理，特别是对个体或独立开发者的影响。
• 关键论据：个体开发者面临的高成本和繁琐程序，Play 商店对新开发者的不友好政策，隐私问题，以及去中心化应用分发的潜在需求。

43849383.article_content:
Google Play’s app marketplace is losing apps.
From the start of 2024 to the present, the Android app marketplace went from hosting about 3.4 million apps worldwide to just around 1.8 million, according to a new analysis by app intelligence provider
Appfigures
. That’s a decline of about 47%, representing a significant purge of the apps that have been available to Android users globally.
The decline is not part of some larger global trend, the firm also notes. During the same period, Apple’s iOS App Store went from hosting 1.6 million apps to now just around 1.64 million apps, for instance — a slight increase.
In Google’s case, the decline in apps could be a relief for Android device owners who have had to sort through scammy, spammy, and otherwise poor-quality apps to find the best ones to install. The reduction could also help developers who have had to fight for visibility.
Over the years, Google Play’s less stringent requirements for app review have led to the marketplace being overrun with lower-quality apps. While Apple continues to enforce strict app review measures before publication, Google often relies on automated checks combined with malware scans to speed up the app-review process. It tends to have a shorter app-review period as a result of its lighter touch in terms of human review.
In July 2024, Google announced it would
raise the minimum quality requirements
for apps, which may have impacted the number of available Play Store app listings.
Instead of only banning broken apps that crashed, wouldn’t install, or run properly, the company said it would begin banning apps that demonstrated “limited functionality and content.” That
included static apps
without app-specific features, such as text-only apps or PDF-file apps. It also included apps that provided little content, like those that only offered a single wallpaper. Additionally, Google banned apps that were designed to do nothing or have no function, which may have been tests or other abandoned developer efforts.
Techcrunch event

Reached for comment, Google confirmed that its new policies were factors here, which also included an expanded set of
verification requirements
,
required app testing
for new personal developer accounts, and
expanded human reviews
to check for apps that try to deceive or defraud users.
In addition, the company pointed to other 2024 investments in AI for threat detection, stronger privacy policies, improved developer tools, and more. As a result, Google
prevented
2.36 million policy-violating apps from being published on its Play Store and banned more than 158,000 developer accounts that had attempted to publish harmful apps, it said.
One factor Google didn’t cite was the new trader status rule enforced by the EU as of this February, which began requiring developers to share their names and addresses in the app’s listing. Those who failed to do so would see their apps removed from EU app stores. (It’s worth pointing out that Apple
also began requiring trader status
information in February and did not see a decline in available apps as a result.)
Appfigures additionally notes it began seeing a decline in the number of apps on the Google Play Store even before the official start of the purge last summer; it doesn’t yet have an explanation for this change. However, the firm says there have been 10,400 releases on Google Play so far this year, up 7.1% year-over-year as of April.

data.title: Future of OSU Open Source Lab in Jeopardy
data.author: aendruk
data.article_summary: 开放源代码实验室（OSL）正面临严峻的资金短缺，可能在2025年晚些时候关闭。由于企业捐赠减少，俄勒冈州立大学（OSU）工程学院（CoE）一直在资助OSL，但因大学预算削减，这一模式难以为继。OSL需要在5月14日前筹集25万美元，以维持运营，其中大部分资金用于支付员工和学生的工资以及其他日常开支。若无法筹集到这笔资金，实验室将被迫关闭。OSL为超过500个开源项目提供托管服务，并在其22年的历史中培养了130多名学生。此外，大学计划淘汰OSL目前使用的数据中心，而OSL缺乏资金更换老化的设备或寻找新的托管地点。当前最紧迫的任务是筹集资金，以确保实验室的持续运营。如能提供帮助，请联系donations@osuosl.org。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Open Source Lab (OSL) 的影响和资金问题

不同观点：
• 支持OSL的观点：
  - 多名用户（ecnahc515, mburns, EMH333, aseipp, gkanai, don-bright）表示OSL对他们的职业发展有重大影响，提供了宝贵的实践经验，特别是在系统管理和开发运营方面。
  - OSL为众多开源项目提供了基础设施支持，包括Drupal、Gentoo Linux、Debian、Fedora等（ecnahc515, gkanai, don-bright）。
  - 一些成功的技术创业公司，如CoreOS，由OSL校友创立，显示了其对科技创业生态的贡献（ecnahc515）。

• 对资金问题的讨论：
  - 有人（nl）质疑为什么不公开最大的赞助商名称，认为这样可以增加透明度和赞誉。
  - 有人（mulderc, Grae）表示愿意捐赠以支持OSL，并鼓励其他人也这样做。
  - 有人（jawilson2）对预算中一名 staff member 占据大部分资金表示担忧，认为150K美元用于一个人60%的时间似乎过多。

• 对行业变化的反思：
  - kev009 提到现代计算行业的“租借模式”使得系统级和物理设备方面的工作机会减少，尽管AI数据中心可能带来一些复兴，但长期前景不明朗。

补充讨论：
• 对OSL独特价值的认可：
  - mburns 和 ecnahc515 强调OSL不仅支持开源项目，还为学生提供了重要的实践经验和教育机会，这在其他地方很难找到。
  
• 对OSL未来的担忧和建议：
  - rdtsc 提到如果关闭OSL，对一些特殊架构如Linux on Z和POWER的支持将失去，建议一些富有的科技巨头可以伸出援手。
  - Grae 指出，OSL需要通过与501(c)(3)组织合作来接受免税捐赠，并提供了具体的捐赠方式。

争议焦点：
• OSL的预算分配，特别是用于一名 staff member 的150K美元，引发了是否过高的讨论。
• 对最大赞助商不公开的质疑，涉及透明度和赞誉问题。

整体来看，评论大多对OSL持积极评价，认为其对开源社区和学生有重要贡献，但对其资金和预算分配有一些争议和建议。

43849271.article_content:
Future of OSL in Jeopardy
by Lance Albertson on Wed, Apr 30 2025
I am writing to inform you about a critical and time-sensitive situation facing the Open Source Lab. Over the past
several years, we have been operating at a deficit due to a decline in corporate donations. While OSUâs College of
Engineering (CoE) has generously filled this gap, recent changes in university funding have led to a significant
reduction in CoEâs budget. As a result, our current funding model is no longer sustainable and CoE needs to find ways
to cut programs.
Earlier this week, I was informed that unless we secure $250,000 in committed funds, the OSL will be forced to shut
down later this year. I have reached out to our largest corporate sponsor and they are working to increase their
support as we update our contract, but that still may not be enough.
For transparency, the $250,000 is broken down into the following roughly:
Staff pay $150k (60%) (1 staff)
Student pay $65k (26%) (8 students)
Other expenses $35k (14%)
Other expenses include items such as hardware, travel, subscription services and other miscellaneous expenses needed to
run the OSL day to day.
If any of you can assist or connect me with potential supporters, please reach out as soon as possible. I need to
provide leadership with an update on any funding changes by
Wednesday, May 14, 2025
. Please reach out directly via
donations@osuosl.org
if youâre able to help us make it through this difficult time.
The OSU Foundation is an IRS 501(c)(3) nonprofit corporation, which provides many donors a tax advantage. Please
contact the OSU Foundation directly if you have questions about your eligibility. You can donate directly to us by
visiting our
donation page
.
OSL provides hosting for over 500 Free and Open Source Projects from all over the world. Over the course of its 22-year
existence, the OSL has mentored over 130 students, many of whom have gone on to create their own companies and work
throughout the larger tech ecosystem.
Some notable milestones over the years include:
Provided hosting for Mozilla Firefox when they needed help in the early days and hosted the release of 1.0
Was the home of the Apache Software Foundation, Linux Foundation, Kernel.org, Mozilla for many years
Offers fast and reliable software mirroring for projects
Currently provides infrastructure hosting for projects such as Drupal, Gentoo Linux, Debian, Fedora, phpBB, OpenID,
Buildroot/Busybox, Inkscape, Cinc and many more!
Virtual machines for x86, aarch64 and ppc64le are used by many projects for CI and other hosted services
Additionally, the university has long-term plans to deprecate the data center where all of our hosting is currently
located. Much of the university hosting has been moved to the cloud or the state data center, and OSU lacks the funds
to replace the aging UPS/HVAC systems. I am actively seeking a new location to host our systems, but finding suitable
data center space on campus has proven to be extremely challenging.
To be clear: OSLâs immediate need is securing additional funding, the data center situation can be worked on later.
Your commitment is crucial for us to move forward. I am available to answer any questions you might have.
Thank you for your continued support!
Lance Albertson, Director

data.title: NYC home prices rise 10% in early 2025
data.author: geox
data.article_summary: 2025年初，纽约市房价同比上涨10%，曼哈顿引领增长，中位售价达$768,000。曼哈顿的Hudson Yards成为最贵社区，中位售价$5.355百万，其他如Little Italy、SoHo等也位列前五。皇后区的Malba中位售价最高，达$1.55百万，而布鲁克林的涨幅最大，尤其是Madison社区，中位售价暴涨145%至$1.25百万。布朗克斯的房价增长最慢，无一社区进入全市前50。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：纽约市房地产市场的价格变化及相关因素

不同观点：
• **[wdpk]** 认为文章标题具有误导性，全市范围内10%的中位数增长没有实际意义。不同社区的中位数价格差异很大，且不同类型的房产（如联排别墅、新开发楼盘、合作公寓等）价格差异显著。他指出，Carroll Gardens的中位价格减半只是因为某季度内销售的房产类型变化，而非整体价格下跌。
  
• **[GlibMonkeyDeath]** 强调房地产市场是本地化的，单个区域的趋势难以代表整体。对比了不同大都市区的房价，指出纽约市的房价虽上升10%，但仍低于洛杉矶/橙县和圣何塞/桑尼维尔。同时提到一些价格较低的城市如克利夫兰和布法罗。

• **[janalsncm]** 推测纽约市的房价趋势可能不会在整个上半年保持，并指出湾区房价也可能因市场波动下跌。他认为高收入人群的资产组合中股票比例较高，股市波动对高端房产市场影响更大。

• **[akoster]** 指出纽约市人口尚未恢复到2020年高点，但租金和房价仍在快速上涨。他提到原因包括临时住所、外国投资者、新建筑不足等，质疑为何人口减少和新建住宅增加未能降低价格。

• **[koolba]** 认为纽约市房价上涨符合逻辑，因为黄金和欧元等国际资产价格上涨，而纽约是国际化城市。

• **[affinepplan]** 认为当前的房价上涨不可持续且不应被接受，几乎所有社会问题都可以追溯到住房供应不足。

• **[ChrisLTD]** 表示纽约市房价仍在上涨，似乎尚未达到市场无法承受的极限。

• **[leflambeur]** 提出纽约市的房价涨幅可能高于美国其他地区，并通过个人观察指出南部郊区的房价自2020年以来上涨了70%，而纽约市的涨幅约为20%。

• **[vondur]** 提到富裕人群迁入纽约市推高了房价，导致中产阶级面临更多竞争。

• **[flerchin]** 指出达拉斯的房价从峰值下降了约10%。

• **[JCM9]** 认为尽管纽约市房价高昂，但相比西海岸仍有吸引力。纽约市在疫情后复苏强劲，许多人希望成为其中一员，且二套房市场强劲，拥有一套纽约市的房产是身份的象征。

• **[margorczynski]** 关注房价上涨是否超过通胀，并指出全球趋势是人口向大城市集中，乡村逐渐衰落。

• **[mupuff1234]** 好奇如果纽约市由新加坡管理会怎样。

• **[ldjkfkdsjnv]** 认为纽约市的租金也失控，但城市仍是地球上最好的地方。

• **[ramesh31]** 强烈建议在低哈德逊河谷购买房地产，认为该地区公共交通便利且房价相对可承受。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于纽约市房价上涨的原因及可持续性，部分评论者认为市场存在泡沫，而另一些人则认为纽约市的吸引力及国际资本流入将继续推高房价。

43849791.article_content:
Real Estate
NYC home prices rise 10% in early 2025, with Manhattan leading and Malba ranking highest in Queens: report
By Ethan Marshall
Posted on
April 29, 2025
Manhattan accounted for the top five neighborhoods in New York City with the highest median sale price during the first quarter of 2025, according to a report from PropertyShark.
Photo via Getty Images
The median sale price across New York City rose 10% year-over-year in the first quarter of 2025, from around $698,000 last year to $768,000 this year, according to a
report
by the real estate database site
PropertyShark
. Several Manhattan neighborhoods had the most significant increases over this period of time among the boroughs included in the study (Staten Island is not included), from $999,000 in 2024 to $1.15 million in 2025.
Manhattan neighborhoods account for the five most expensive places in New York City during the first quarter of 2025. Hudson Yards is the most expensive place to live, with a median sale price of $5.355 million, followed by Little Italy at $4.593 million, SoHo at $3.85 million, TriBeCa at $3.3 million and Hudson Square at $2.6 million. Hudson Square also had the sharpest percentage jump in median sale price in the borough and the third-highest among the top 50 neighborhoods, with a 61% increase from $1.615 million last year.
Queens had very little growth in its median sale price compared to that of Manhattan. There was just a 6% increase in the World’s Borough, from $549,000 last year to $581,000 this year. There was still a strong presence of neighborhoods in the borough among the top 50 highest median sale prices in New York City, with 11 appearing on the list.
Malba
ranked the highest, at 11th overall with a median sale price of $1.55 million.
Close
